content.content:
1	---
2	title: "Record with record_screen"
3	description: "How an agent records the screen, a camera or a voice-over for a set time and lands it in a project: every argument, answer and refusal."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	`record_screen` is **File ▸ New Recording…** without the panel. An agent says how many seconds to record, the call runs for that long, and the recording lands in the project the way one made with the panel does. There's no countdown, and the tool never asks for a permission.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
12	  tools="record_screen"
13	  needs={[
14	    'Screen Recording permission, for a screen recording',
15	    'Microphone, Camera or Input Monitoring, only when the call uses them',
16	    'A person has to give each permission first',
17	  ]}
18	/>
19	
20	## Record the screen
21	
22	The smallest call names only `seconds`:
23	
24	```json
25	{ "seconds": 30 }
26	```
27	
28	That records the main display for 30 seconds with its system sound, leaves Frame Job's own windows out of the picture, and lands the movie at the playhead of the front project. A recording then goes through these stages:
29	
30	- **It starts at once.** There's no countdown and no panel.
31	- **It writes to disk.** The file goes to `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`, named for example `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov`, and it's never stored inside the project. A name that's already taken gets ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on.
32	- **It lands.** The movie becomes ordinary media, and a clip goes at the playhead on the front track of whatever is open, a [nest](/mcp/nests/) included. When that track has no room there, Frame Job adds a new track in front of everything. This is one undo step, **Add Recording**.
33	- **It answers.** The call returns once the recording is finished, imported and placed. See [What it answers](#what-it-answers).
34	
35	With no project open, the recording opens as a new untitled project instead, and `landed` reads `new_project`. Its canvas takes the movie's size and `rate`. Later calls address that project with `project` set to the recording's path, which is the path `get_project` reports for it. If the target project closes while the recording runs, the same thing happens and the note says so.
36	
37	Only one recording runs at a time, whoever started it. A second one is refused with "A recording is already in progress."
38	
39	:::note
40	The built-in [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) can't call `record_screen`. Recording stays with a person at the Record button, or an agent connected from outside.
41	:::
42	
43	[Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) has the landing in full, and it's the same for both.
44	
45	## Choose a source
46	
47	`source` says what's recorded.
48	
49	| `source` | What it records | Files |
50	| --- | --- | --- |
51	| `screen` | A display or a window. The default. | `Screen Recording <date> at <time>.mov` |
52	| `voice_over` | The default microphone alone, with no picture. | `Voice-over <date> at <time>.m4a` |
53	| `camera` | A camera alone, with no screen. | `Camera Recording <date> at <time>.mov` |
54	
55	An argument the source can't use is refused by name, not ignored. A JSON null counts as not given. This is what each source takes:
56	
57	| Argument | `screen` | `voice_over` | `camera` |
58	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
59	| `seconds`, `project`, `path`, `place`, `enhance` | Yes | Yes | Yes |
60	| `microphone` | Yes | Implied, and `false` is refused | Yes |
61	| `rate` | Yes | Yes, for a new project's canvas | Refused |
62	| `camera`, `camera_format` | Yes, [beside the screen](#record-a-camera-beside-the-screen) | Refused | Yes |
63	| `camera_layout`, `camera_cutout` | Yes, with `camera` | Refused | Refused |
64	| `display`, `window`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows` | Yes | Refused | Refused |
65	| `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `cursor`, `keys` | Yes | Refused | Refused |
66	| `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing` | Yes | Refused | Refused |
67	
68	## The arguments
69	
70	Only `seconds` is required. The sections further down cover the arguments for [voice-overs](#record-a-voice-over), [cameras](#record-a-camera-alone) and the [steps after landing](#run-steps-after-it-lands).
71	
72	### Length and source
73	
74	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
75	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
76	| `seconds` | number | Required | How long to record, from 1 to 600 seconds. It's wall-clock time, so a [pause](#a-person-can-pause-or-stop-it) shortens what's recorded. |
77	| `source` | `screen`, `voice_over` or `camera` | `screen` | What's recorded. See [Choose a source](#choose-a-source). |
78	
79	### Display or window
80	
81	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
82	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
83	| `display` | whole number, 0 or more | `0` | Which display, as an index into the displays that can be shared, 0 being the main one. Can't be used with `window`. |
84	| `window` | whole number | None | The id of one window to record on its own, at that window's own size, instead of a display. Can't be used with `display`. |
85	| `include_framejob_windows` | boolean | `false` | Puts Frame Job's own windows, the editor and the preview, in a display recording. By default they're left out. With `window` it changes nothing. Frame Job's own sound stays out either way. |
86	| `size` | `nominal` or `best`, in any case | `nominal` | `nominal` records a display's point size, and `best` its pixel size, twice the points on a Retina display. An odd dimension is rounded up to even. |
87	| `rate` | `30` or `60` | `60` | The most frames a second the file may hold, and the canvas rate of a new project the recording opens as. |
88	
89	A screen recording's frame rate is whatever the screen did, because a frame arrives only when something changes. A mostly still screen reports a low, fractional rate. That's the file and not a fault, and the picture holds its last frame to the end of the sound.
90	
91	### Sound
92	
93	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
94	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
95	| `system_audio` | boolean | `true` | Records what the Mac plays as the movie's one stereo 48 kHz track. It takes in every app but Frame Job, so the timeline can play meanwhile and stay out of it. `false` writes a movie with no audio track, and `has_audio` reads false. |
96	| `microphone` | boolean | `false` | Also records the default microphone, to a second file beside the movie named `<movie name> (Microphone).m4a`. |
97	
98	The microphone's file lands as its own clip on a new track at the back named **Microphone**, lined up with the picture by the measured `mic_offset`. When the microphone began first and there's no room for it there, the clip's head is trimmed rather than the clip landing late.
99	
100	A microphone that fails doesn't fail the recording. The picture lands, that stretch has no `mic_path`, and `mic_problem` and the note say why. See [System audio and the microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/).
101	
102	### Pointer and keys
103	
104	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
105	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
106	| `cursor` | `separate` or `in_picture` | `separate` | `separate` keeps the pointer out of the movie, and Frame Job draws it on the clip from the cursor file, where you can restyle it. `in_picture` has macOS burn the pointer into the movie. |
107	| `show_clicks` | boolean | `false` | Shows each mouse click. With `in_picture`, a circle is drawn around each click into the movie. With `separate`, the clips land with click ripples on, drawn by Frame Job. |
108	| `keys` | `off` or `shortcuts` | `off` | `shortcuts` writes keyboard shortcuts into the cursor files, and needs the Input Monitoring permission. |
109	
110	Every display or window recording writes a cursor file beside each movie, named `<movie name>.fjcursor`, holding the pointer's path, its clicks and scrolls. A problem with it never fails the recording. `segments` reports it as `cursor_problem`, and the note repeats it. A `separate` stretch with no cursor file has no pointer at all, and the note ends "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."
111	
112	With `keys: "shortcuts"`, the file records each shortcut pressed with ⌘ or ⌃, or with ⌥ and an arrow, Delete, Forward Delete, Return, Enter, Tab or Esc, spelled like `cmd+shift+4`. Every other key is a mark of the time alone, never which key was typed. Nothing is written while an app holds secure input. See [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) and [The cursor in a recording](/recording/cursor/).
113	
114	### Where it goes
115	
116	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
117	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
118	| `path` | string | `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings` | A folder to record into, created if it doesn't exist. It names the folder and never the file, and the answer's `path` is the file that was written. A blank string means the default folder. |
119	| `project` | string | The front project | The open project to land in, as `get_project` reports its path. One that names nothing open is refused, and it never turns into a new project. |
120	| `place` | boolean | `true` | Puts clips on the timeline, in one undo step with the media. `false` adds the recording to the media list only, and the note says to place it with `add_clip`. |
121	
122	In a new project `place: false` has no effect, because the picture is the document. Its clips are on the timeline, one for each stretch and the first at 0, and the note says so.
123	
124	## Record a voice-over
125	
126	`source: "voice_over"` records the default microphone alone, as the panel's **Microphone Only** does. `microphone: true` is implied. The only permission it reads is the Microphone one, and it looks nothing up.
127	
128	Each stretch between pauses is its own `.m4a` file. The files land touching, from the playhead, on one new track at the back named **Microphone**, in one undo step, **Add Recording**. In a new project the first file is the document, 1920 × 1080 at `rate`, and later files touch it on its one track.
129	
130	The answer's `path` is the first `.m4a`, its `width` and `height` are 0, and it has no `mic_path`. A microphone that stops on its own ends the voice-over, what it wrote lands, and `mic_problem` and the note say so.
131	
132	See [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/).
133	
134	## Record a camera alone
135	
136	`source: "camera"` records one camera, with no screen, and lands it as a screen recording's picture lands. It reads the Camera permission and never the Screen Recording one. `microphone: true` adds the default microphone as a second file, as for a screen.
137	
138	Recording starts once the camera has settled at its frame rate, which takes up to a second, and `seconds` counts from its first frame. While it runs, the panel's **Preview** reads "The camera is recording." The movie holds no sound, so `has_audio` is false. In a new project the canvas is the file's size at the format's frame rate, rounded.
139	
140	### Choose the camera and its format
141	
142	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
143	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
144	| `camera` | string | The default camera with `source: "camera"`, none with `source: "screen"` | A camera's unique id, or its name in any case. Blank means none. |
145	| `camera_format` | string | `best` | The format to record at, in any case: `1920x1080@30`, or `1920x1080` for that size's highest frame rate, or `best`. Blank or null means `best`. |
146	
147	The default camera is the Mac's preferred camera, then the first built-in one, then the first connected. `best` is the largest size wider than tall that runs at 30 fps or more, at its highest frame rate.
148	
149	An unknown camera is refused with a list of every camera connected, by name and id. With none connected the answer is "No camera is connected." A format the camera doesn't have is refused with a list of its formats.
150	
151	The answer carries `camera`, with the camera's `name`, `id` and `format`, spelled like `1920x1080@30`. It adds `problem` when the camera stopped on its own, which ends the recording with `stopped_by: "system_stopped"` and lands what it wrote, and `note` when the camera hadn't settled by the time recording began. The answer's note repeats both.
152	
153	See [Record a camera](/recording/record-a-camera/).
154	
155	## Record a camera beside the screen
156	
157	`source: "screen"` with `camera` records that camera at the same time as the screen, for a talking head over a screencast. It's the panel's **Record the camera too** box, and `camera_format` works as it does for a camera alone.
158	
159	Each stretch gets a camera movie named after its screen movie, like `Screen Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33 (Camera).mov`. The camera files land in the same undo step as the screen, on one new track named **Camera** in front of the screen's. Each camera clip starts where its screen clip starts, moved by that stretch's measured `camera_offset`. A camera usually starts a little before the screen, and then the clip's first frames are trimmed rather than the clip starting early. A camera clip never starts before its screen clip, and never overlaps the camera clip before it.
160	
161	With `place: false` the camera files are added to the media list only, with no clip and no **Camera** track. In a new project the first movie is the document, and its camera is one undo step: **Add Camera**, or **Add Camera and Microphone** with a microphone, for a recording that wasn't paused.
162	
163	The Camera permission is checked before the Screen Recording one. See [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/).
164	
165	### Lay the camera out
166	
167	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
168	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
169	| `camera_layout` | see below | `corner_square` | How each camera clip lands, laid out from its first frame with its stretch's screen clip, as the panel's **Layout** does. |
170	| `camera_cutout` | boolean | `false` | Runs [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) on the camera clips right after the landing, as the panel's **Remove the camera's background when it lands** box does. |
171	
172	| `camera_layout` | Panel's name | What you get |
173	| --- | --- | --- |
174	| `corner_square` | Corner | The bottom-right corner, scaled to fit a box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, inside the 90 % safe area. |
175	| `corner_rounded` | Rounded Corner | The same corner with rounded edges. |
176	| `corner_circle` | Circle | The same corner as a circle. |
177	| `side_by_side` | Side by Side | The screen and the camera next to each other. |
178	| `camera_full` | Camera Full | The camera fills the canvas. |
179	
180	The layout reaches no further than the later end of the two clips. When a stretch's screen clip is missing, or isn't playing where its camera starts, that camera goes in the bottom-right corner instead. Either way it stays an ordinary clip you can move. [Camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/) has the rest.
181	
182	Both arguments are refused without `camera`, with `source: "voice_over"` or `"camera"`, and with `place: false`. All of that is answered before any permission is read. For example: "With source screen, camera_layout needs camera — name the camera to record beside the screen."
183	
184	## Run steps after it lands
185	
186	These arguments run a command over the recording once it has landed. Each is its own undo step, so undoing one keeps the recording, and they run in the order of this table. The landing itself is the same with or without them.
187	
188	| Argument | What it runs | On which clips | Undo step | Needs |
189	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
190	| `camera_cutout` | Remove Background | The camera clips | **Remove Background** | `camera`, `place: true` |
191	| `enhance` | `enhance_voice` at −16 LUFS | The microphone's clips, or a voice-over's | **Enhance Voice** | `microphone: true` or `source: "voice_over"`, `place: true` |
192	| `auto_zoom` | `auto_zoom` | The screen clips | **Auto Zoom** | `place: true` |
193	| `shortcut_overlays` | `add_shortcut_overlays` | The screen clips | **Add Shortcut Overlays** | `place: true`, `keys: "shortcuts"` |
194	| `speed_up_typing` | `speed_up_typing` | The screen clips | **Speed Up Typing** | `place: true`, `keys: "shortcuts"` |
195	
196	All default to `false`. The last three are the panel's **When it lands:** boxes, **Zoom in on clicks**, **Show shortcuts** and **Speed up typing**. `enhance` is its **Enhance the microphone when it lands** box. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).
197	
198	The screen clips are the clips of the recording's movies that have a cursor file. `enhance` never touches the picture, a camera or the system audio.
199	
200	### What they wait for
201	
202	The call stays open while these run, and `project` in the answer is read after them.
203	
204	- `enhance` waits for the microphone's loudness and speech to be analysed, up to 5 minutes.
205	- `speed_up_typing` waits for the clips' speech to be detected, up to 5 minutes.
206	- Those two and the other two tools also wait while the project is busy, up to 5 minutes: a drag is under way, or a different nest is open from the one the recording landed in.
207	- `camera_cutout` waits for nothing, and runs straight after the landing.
208	
209	### The values they use
210	
211	They run at the tools' own defaults, never at what the sheets last remembered.
212	
213	| Step | Values |
214	| --- | --- |
215	| `enhance` | −16 LUFS. Call [`enhance_voice`](/mcp/tools-audio/#enhance_voice) afterwards for another target. |
216	| `auto_zoom` | Zoom ×2, Lead 0.6 s, Stay 2.5 s, Follow the cursor while zoomed on, Zoom on typing on, Replace existing zooms off, Motion blur 50 %. |
217	| `shortcut_overlays` | Bottom, dark, 1.5 s. |
218	| `speed_up_typing` | ×4 for stretches of 3 s or more, Keep pitch on. A speed-up that leaves a clip silent above ×12 is applied, and says so in `audio_note`. |
219	
220	### What each one answers
221	
222	Each step adds its own answer to the call's answer, under its name, or a sentence under `<name>_error` saying why it didn't run. The recording stays either way.
223	
224	| Key | Holds |
225	| --- | --- |
226	| `camera_cutout` | `clips`, the clips that were cut out. |
227	| `camera_cutout_error` | "No camera clip landed on the timeline, so Remove Background did not run." |
228	| `enhance` | What `enhance_voice` answers. |
229	| `enhance_error` | That no microphone clip landed, that it wasn't ready to measure within 5 minutes, that the call was stopped first, or `enhance_voice`'s own reason. |
230	| `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing` | What each tool answers. |
231	| `auto_zoom_error`, `shortcut_overlays_error`, `speed_up_typing_error` | That no screen clip with a cursor file landed, that the project was busy or the speech wasn't detected within 5 minutes, that the call was stopped first, or the tool's own reason. |
232	
233	Among the last three, one that its tool turns down doesn't stop the next. When no screen clip landed, a wait runs out or the call is stopped, none of the remaining ones run, and each gets its own sentence.
234	
235	## It never asks for a permission
236	
237	`record_screen` reads each permission and never requests one. It never shows a system prompt, never opens the window picker and never opens System Settings. A person grants them in the panel, usually by pressing **Record** in **File ▸ New Recording…** once. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).
238	
239	| Permission | When it's read | What a missing one answers |
240	| --- | --- | --- |
241	| Screen Recording | Any `screen` recording | "Screen Recording is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording, then relaunch." |
242	| Microphone | `microphone: true` or `source: "voice_over"` | "The microphone is not granted to Frame Job (status: denied)." and the Microphone pane. With status `notDetermined`, it says to press Record in **File ▸ New Recording…** once. The status may also read `restricted`. |
243	| Camera | `source: "camera"` or `camera` | "The camera is not granted to Frame Job (status: denied)." and the Camera pane. With status `notDetermined`, it says to press Record with the Camera source once. |
244	| Input Monitoring | `keys: "shortcuts"` | "Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring." |
245	
246	A Frame Job launched from a shell runs under the terminal's permissions, not its own. Each of these answers then also names the launching process by its pid, and says the permission that counts is that application's, or to relaunch with `open -a "Frame Job"`.
247	
248	:::caution
249	macOS periodically asks whether to keep letting Frame Job record, and neither Frame Job nor the tool can see that alert. A capture waiting behind it looks like a hang. When a start or a finish times out, the answer says an alert may be waiting on the screen. Answer it and call again.
250	:::
251	
252	## What's checked first
253	
254	Refusals come in a fixed order, with the caller's own mistakes first, so a mistake is answered even with no permission at all.
255	
256	1. `seconds` missing or outside 1 to 600.
257	2. `source` unknown, then the arguments that source can't take, then `microphone: false` with a voice-over.
258	3. `display` with `window`, or a `display` or `window` that isn't a valid number.
259	4. `rate` or `size` outside its values.
260	5. `keys` or `cursor` outside its values.
261	6. `enhance` without a microphone, then with `place: false`.
262	7. `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing`, in that order, each with `place: false`, and the last two without `keys: "shortcuts"`.
263	8. `camera_layout` outside its values, then `camera_layout` and `camera_cutout` with `place: false`.
264	9. The Microphone permission.
265	10. The Input Monitoring permission.
266	11. A `project` that names nothing open.
267	12. For a camera, the camera lookup, then `camera_format`, then the Camera permission.
268	13. For a screen, the Screen Recording permission.
269	14. The display or window lookup. A window that can't be shared answers "No window with id 123 is shareable." An index past the last display answers "display must be 0…1 (got 3); 2 displays are shareable."
270	
271	When the console is locked or every display is asleep, step 14 answers "No display is shareable right now — the console is locked or every display is asleep; nothing can be recorded until one is."
272	
273	After those, a call with a microphone needs a default microphone, or it answers "No microphone is available." Then the recording starts.
274	
275	## How long the call takes
276	
277	| Stage | How long |
278	| --- | --- |
279	| Starting | Up to 20 seconds, then "The recording did not start within 20 s." |
280	| Recording | `seconds`, plus about a second to start and finish. |
281	| Finishing | Up to about 75 s more if the files are slow to close, and 60 s more for each further stretch of a paused recording. |
282	| Finishing, with a camera beside the screen | Up to about 105 s more, and 90 s more for each further stretch, because each camera file is read too. |
283	| Landing | Up to 20 seconds, while a drag in the target project ends. |
284	| [Steps after landing](#what-they-wait-for) | Up to 5 minutes for each wait. |
285	
286	A finish that times out answers with every movie it still holds, then the camera files, because they may yet finish on their own. If a drag outlasts its wait, the answer names the files too, which are on disk either way:
287	
288	"The recording was saved at `<path>` but could not be added: …"
289	
290	Calls run one at a time, so a recording holds up the next call until it answers. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).
291	
292	## A person can pause or stop it
293	
294	While an agent records, the same [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) appears as for the panel, so a person at the Mac can pause, resume or stop it. **File ▸ Pause Recording** and **File ▸ Stop Recording** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>) work too. An agent has no tool to pause or resume.
295	
296	- **Stop** ends the call early and the recording still lands, with `stopped_by: "stopped"` and a `duration` shorter than `seconds`. That's the same value the tool's own stop gives, so the short `duration` is what tells the two apart.
297	- **Pause** shortens what the call records, because `seconds` keeps running. The paused time is in no file, and `pauses` counts the presses, including a pause with no resume before the stop.
298	
299	A paused recording is a sequence of files, one for each stretch between a start or a resume and a pause or the stop. Each is named by its own start time and carries its own microphone file. Every stretch lands as its own clip on one track, touching the one before, and each microphone file as its own clip on the **Microphone** track at its own offset.
300	
301	## What it answers
302	
303	Times are ticks, 600,000 to the second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). Most top-level keys describe the first stretch, the recording's own file.
304	
305	| Key | What it holds |
306	| --- | --- |
307	| `path` | The first stretch's file, the one a new project is addressed by. |
308	| `duration` | The total recorded across every stretch. |
309	| `width`, `height`, `fps` | The first stretch's picture size and frame rate, with `fps` as `[num, den]`. |
310	| `has_audio`, `audio_tracks` | What that movie holds. `audio_tracks` is 1 with system audio, else 0. The microphone is never a track of the movie. |
311	| `mic_offset` | Always present, and 0 with no microphone. The measured lead in ticks, positive when the picture began after the microphone. |
312	| `mic_path`, `mic_duration` | The first stretch's microphone file, when it landed. |
313	| `mic_problem` | Every stretch's microphone sentence, joined. It can stand beside a `mic_path` when a later stretch failed. |
314	| `media`, `clip`, `mic_media`, `mic_clip` | The first stretch's ids. There's no `clip` or `mic_clip` with `place: false`. |
315	| `camera` | The camera used, as in [Choose the camera and its format](#choose-the-camera-and-its-format). |
316	| `pauses` | How many times Pause was pressed, 0 when never. |
317	| `segments` | Always present, one entry for each file, in order. Exactly one for a recording never paused. |
318	| `stopped_by` | `stopped` for the tool's own stop and a person's Stop from Frame Job. `user_stopped` for macOS's own screen-recording indicator. `system_stopped` for a display that slept or a camera that stopped on its own. |
319	| `landed` | `document` or `new_project`. |
320	| `unreadable` | Any stretches left out. See below. |
321	| `note` | Present when there's something to say. |
322	| `project` | The usual project summary. |
323	| `new_media`, `new_clips`, `new_tracks` | The ids made, as every edit reports them, when it landed in an open project. `new_tracks` appears when a track was added. `scope` and `document_ops` appear when it landed inside a nest. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/). |
324	
325	Each entry of `segments` carries these keys. A screen recording's frame rate differs between stretches, so each has its own.
326	
327	| Key | What it holds |
328	| --- | --- |
329	| `path`, `duration`, `width`, `height`, `fps` | This stretch's file. |
330	| `started_at` | When this stretch began, in UTC to the millisecond, like `2026-09-12T13:04:22.417Z`. |
331	| `mic_offset`, `mic_path`, `mic_duration`, `mic_problem` | As at the top level, for this stretch. |
332	| `media`, `clip`, `mic_media`, `mic_clip` | This stretch's ids, when known. |
333	| `camera_path`, `camera_duration`, `camera_offset` | This stretch's camera file, when it landed. `camera_offset` is in ticks, positive when the camera began after the screen. |
334	| `camera_problem`, `camera_note` | What went wrong with this stretch's camera, when anything did. The note repeats them. |
335	| `camera_media`, `camera_clip` | The camera's ids, when known. |
336	| `cursor_path`, `cursor_image` | This stretch's cursor file, when one was written. `cursor_image` reads `none` because no cursor image is recorded. |
337	| `cursor_problem` | Why the file wasn't written, or holds only the geometry the screen had when the stretch began. |
338	
339	### When a stretch won't read
340	
341	A stretch whose movie won't read, such as an empty file from a pause straight after a resume, is left out rather than failing the recording. The readable stretches land, and `unreadable` lists each one left out, with its `path`, its `kept_files` still on disk and the `reason`. When its microphone file reads, the entry adds `mic_path` and `mic_duration`, and `mic_media` and `mic_clip` when known, and that microphone lands in the slot the picture would have had. A camera file from such a stretch stays on disk, named in `kept_files`, and doesn't land.
342	
343	Only a recording with no readable movie at all fails, and it names every file.
344	
345	## Undo a recording
346	
347	In an open project, one undo removes every stretch's media and clips and leaves the files on disk, as undoing Add Media… does.
348	
349	A recording that opened as a new project has no undo step for its first picture, because that picture is the document. Whatever came with it is one undo step, which leaves the first picture alone in the document:
350	
351	| What came with it | Undo step |
352	| --- | --- |
353	| A microphone, on a recording never paused | **Add Microphone** |
354	| A camera, on a recording never paused | **Add Camera** |
355	| A camera and a microphone, on a recording never paused | **Add Camera and Microphone** |
356	| Only click ripples, on a recording never paused | **Cursor Clicks** |
357	| Later stretches of a paused recording, with all their files | **Add Recording Segments** |
358	
359	[Steps after landing](#run-steps-after-it-lands) undo first, one at a time, last first.

5	
6	Frame Job gives an agent 125 tools. This page names every one and links to its full reference, and says how a client can read what each one takes.
7	
8	## The tool catalog
9	
10	The 125 tools come in two kinds.
11	
12	- **69 edit tools.** Each makes one kind of edit to the project, as one undo step. These also take `scope`, which aims the edit inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/) by the nest's id.
13	- **56 app tools.** These work with files, read things, change what the app is showing, or run a whole command such as `record_screen` or `make_vertical_version`.
14	
15	Every tool takes `project`, which says which open project it acts on. Leave it out for the front project. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).
16	
17	## How arguments are published
18	
19	Each tool publishes its arguments as JSON Schema, in the `inputSchema` of `tools/list`. That's where a client reads every argument's name, its kind, its closed list of values, its bounds and which arguments are required. The helper answers `tools/list` even when Frame Job isn't running. See [The helper and the socket](/mcp/helper-and-socket/).
20	
21	Each tool's description says what it's for and what it answers, and the client shows that to the model. An argument that isn't in the schema is refused by name before the tool runs, in a sentence listing what the tool does take: "trim_start does not take at. It takes clip, to, project and scope."
22	
23	A few arguments read differently from what their kind suggests:
24	
25	| Argument | What's different |
26	| --- | --- |
27	| Every boolean | May also be sent as the string `"true"`, `"1"`, `"false"` or `"0"`. |
28	| `text` on `add_text_clip`, `shape` on `add_shape_clip` | May be a plain string: the words, or the kind of shape. |
29	| `kind` on `set_transition`, `region` on `add_zoom_action` | Must be sent even when null, because null means something: no transition, or zoom back out. |
30	| `rate` on `set_speed` and `add_speed_ramp` | Published as ×0.1 to ×1000. A rate outside that is brought into range, not refused. Zero or less is refused. |
31	| `fps` on `set_canvas` | Each of its two numbers must be at least 1. |
32	| `clips` on every tool, `groups` on `paste_attributes`, `ranges` on `ripple_delete_ranges` and `copy_pieces` | Refused when empty, by name. |
33	| `at` on `split`, `paste`, `freeze_frame` and `add_marker` | Optional. It takes the playhead when left out. |
34	| `focus` on `switch_layout` | May be null or left out, and the tool then fills it from the camera's cached person masks. |
35	
36	Four tools refuse a call that names nothing to change, so they need at least one of their optional arguments: `set_track`, `set_marker`, `set_canvas` and `set_transition_style`.
37	
38	Frame Job fills a few values itself, from what only it can read, so the tools don't publish them and sending one is refused: a graphic's `schema`, a relinked file's details, and the faces and turns `reframe_clip` follows.

132	        _ wanted: String?, format wantedFormat: String?, in cameras: [CameraDeviceFacts],
133	        preferredID: String?, status: AVAuthorizationStatus
134	    ) throws -> CameraPick {
135	        let index: Int?
136	        if let wanted {
137	            index = CameraDevices.match(wanted, in: cameras)
138	        } else {
139	            index = CameraDevices.defaultIndex(in: cameras, preferredID: preferredID)
140	        }
141	        guard let index else {

156	            throw ToolError(message: RecordingGrant.cameraRefusal(status))

201	/// The `RecorderStatusItem` and the 1 Hz timer that ticks its label, for a
202	/// recording `record_screen` started — so a person at the machine can pause,
203	/// resume and stop an agent's recording from the menu bar as they can the
204	/// panel's (R2d). MAIN THREAD throughout: `show` is hopped there after the
205	/// start lands, `remove` runs inside `onFinish` (which the recorder calls on
206	/// main) and on the tool's own finish timeout; `ended` makes the two
207	/// orderings safe, because a recording that concluded before the hop to
208	/// `show` must put nothing up that nothing will take down. The timer is
209	/// added to main's run loop in `.common` modes and invalidated there.
210	///
211	/// The three closures go straight to `ScreenRecorder.shared`. Stop freezes
212	/// the item, then is `stop()` with no completion — a join, landed by the
213	/// tool's own `onFinish`; `record`'s span-end stop freezes it the same way.
214	/// Pause and Resume are `pause()` / `resume()` under `try?`: the menu offers
215	/// each only in the state that accepts it, so the one refusal possible is a
216	/// race with the recording's own end, with no panel to say it in. The flip
217	/// is the recorder's: `show` observes its `pauseDidChangeNotification`
218	/// (synchronous on main, where `pause()` / `resume()` run) and calls
219	/// `tick()`, so the menu flips AT a pause or resume from ANY door — this
220	/// menu, the panel's, File ▸ Pause Recording — and not at the timer's next
221	/// turn (the item rebuilds its menu only when `paused` changes; #181).
222	/// `show` also observes `finishingDidBeginNotification` and calls `freeze()`,
223	/// so any stop, from any door, freezes the tool's item (#193). `remove`
224	/// takes both observers down. The SPAN is wall clock, unchanged: a
225	/// pause from the menu bar shortens what was recorded, and the result's
226	/// `pauses` and `duration` say so.
227	final class RecordingToolChrome {
228	    private var item: RecorderStatusItem?
229	    private var timer: Timer?
230	    private var ended = false
231	    private var observer: NSObjectProtocol?
232	    private var finishObserver: NSObjectProtocol?
233	
234	    init() {}
235	
236	    @available(*, unavailable)
237	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
238	        fatalError("RecordingToolChrome does not support NSCoder")
239	    }
240	
241	    /// MAIN. A no-op once ended, once showing, or for a recorder neither
242	    /// recording nor paused (a pending stop moved it on before the hop). A
243	    /// PAUSED recorder is ADMITTED: the item is then what offers Resume.
244	    func show(_ recorder: ScreenRecorder) {
245	        guard !ended, item == nil, recorder.state == .recording || recorder.state == .paused
246	        else { return }
247	        let item = RecorderStatusItem(
248	            keys: recorder.recordsKeys,
249	            onPause: {
250	                _ = try? ScreenRecorder.shared.pause()
251	            },
252	            onResume: {
253	                _ = try? ScreenRecorder.shared.resume()
254	            },
255	            onStop: { [weak self] in
256	                self?.freeze()
257	                ScreenRecorder.shared.stop()
258	            })
259	        item.show()
260	        observer = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
261	            forName: ScreenRecorder.pauseDidChangeNotification, object: recorder, queue: nil
262	        ) { [weak self] _ in self?.tick() }
263	        finishObserver = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
264	            forName: ScreenRecorder.finishingDidBeginNotification, object: recorder, queue: nil
265	        ) { [weak self] _ in self?.freeze() }
266	        self.item = item
267	        tick()
268	        // `.common` modes, the panel's rule (`RecorderStatusItem`'s doc): under
269	        // an open status-item menu a default-mode timer does not fire.
270	        let tick = Timer(timeInterval: 1, repeats: true) { [weak self] _ in self?.tick() }
271	        RunLoop.main.add(tick, forMode: .common)
272	        timer = tick
273	    }
274	
275	    /// MAIN. The recorder's elapsed — frozen while paused — and whether it
276	    /// is paused, into the item; a no-op once the item is down.
277	    private func tick() {
278	        guard let item else { return }
279	        let recorder = ScreenRecorder.shared
280	        item.update(elapsed: recorder.elapsed, paused: recorder.isPaused)
281	    }
282	
283	    /// MAIN. A stop is under way: the item holds its mark and time through
284	    /// the finish (`RecorderStatusItem.freeze`), or the next tick — `isPaused`
285	    /// false once finishing — would flip a paused ❚❚ back to the coral dot.
286	    func freeze() { item?.freeze() }
287	
288	    /// MAIN. Idempotent.
289	    func remove() {
290	        ended = true
291	        if let observer { NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(observer) }
292	        observer = nil
293	        if let finishObserver { NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(finishObserver) }
294	        finishObserver = nil
295	        timer?.invalidate()
296	        timer = nil
297	        item?.remove()
298	        item = nil
299	    }
300	}

305	/// finished recording takes — a document through `editResult`, a new project

307	/// `AgentServer+Recording.swift` at the 400-line cap, landed alone before
308	/// camera + screen grows the tool; nothing in either body changed, and
309	/// `private` → internal is the whole cost, because a `private` extension

315	    /// SERVER THREAD. A target document mid-drag is not committed over the
316	    /// gesture's base handle (`RecordingLanding.placement` refuses by name);
317	    /// the panel retries from a half-second timer bounded at forty tries,
318	    /// and this polls `isLiveEditing` through `onMain` at that interval and
319	    /// bound BY NAME, so the two doors cannot drift. A gesture outlasting
320	    /// the bound still reaches `placement`'s refusal, which names the file;
321	    /// a `.newProject` target or a closed document has nothing to wait for.
322	    func awaitGestureEnd(_ destination: RecordingDestination) {
323	        for _ in 0..<RecorderPanelController.landingRetryLimit {
324	            let dragging = onMain { () -> Bool in
325	                guard case .document(let document) = RecordingLanding.resolve(destination)
326	                else { return false }
327	                return document.isLiveEditing
328	            }
329	            guard dragging else { return }
330	            Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: RecorderPanelController.landingRetryInterval)
331	        }
332	    }

334	    /// MAIN. The two doors: a document through `editResult` (one undo step,
335	    /// the `created` ids, the scope landing); a new project through
336	    /// `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`, which does everything. Every
337	    /// throw past this point is `savedButNotAdded`'s: every segment's files
338	    /// exist. The result is `recordingFields` over the segments plus the ids
339	    /// each door knows them by (the placement's lists, predicted before the
340	    /// commit; the new project's snapshot, read by path), and `note` is the
341	    /// door's sentences in order: `place: false`, a closed target, what the
342	    /// landing could NOT place (each naming its file), then `resultNotes(result)`.
343	    /// Answers the document it landed in beside the answer, for
344	    /// `landAndEnhance`.
345	    func land(_ result: RecordingResult, place: Bool) throws
346	        -> (answer: String, document: ProjectDocument)
347	    {
348	        var fields: [String: Any]
349	        var notes: [String] = []
350	        switch RecordingLanding.resolve(result.choice.destination) {
351	        case .document(let document):
352	            let placement: RecordingLanding.Placement
353	            do {
354	                placement = try RecordingLanding.placement(result, in: document, place: place)
355	            } catch {
356	                throw Self.savedButNotAdded(result, error)
357	            }
358	            fields = Self.recordingFields(
359	                result, ids: Self.documentIds(result, placement: placement),
360	                leftOutIds: Self.documentLeftOutIds(result, placement: placement))
361	            fields["landed"] = "document"
362	            if !place {
363	                notes.append(
364	                    "The recording is in the project's media list but not on the timeline — "
365	                        + "place it with add_clip {track, media, at}.")
366	            }
367	            notes.append(contentsOf: placement.notes)
368	            notes.append(contentsOf: Self.resultNotes(result))
369	            if !notes.isEmpty { fields["note"] = notes.joined(separator: " ") }
370	            let answer: String
371	            do {
372	                answer = try editResult(document, RecordingLanding.actionName, placement.ops, fields)
373	            } catch {
374	                throw Self.savedButNotAdded(result, error)
375	            }
376	            // `editResult` commits and does not build caches; `importMedia`
377	            // calls this after its own commit for the same reason.
378	            document.generateCaches()
379	            return (answer, document)
380	        case .newProject:
381	            let document: ProjectDocument
382	            var landingNotes: [String] = []
383	            do {
384	                let landing = try ProjectDocument.untitled(around: result)
385	                document = landing.document
386	                landingNotes = landing.notes
387	            } catch {
388	                throw Self.savedButNotAdded(result, error)
389	            }
390	            fields = Self.recordingFields(
391	                result, ids: Self.newProjectIds(result, in: document),
392	                leftOutIds: Self.newProjectLeftOutIds(result, in: document))
393	            fields["landed"] = "new_project"
394	            if result.choice.destination != .newProject {
395	                notes.append(
396	                    "The target document closed while the recording ran, so it opened as a "
397	                        + "new project instead.")
398	            }
399	            if !place {
400	                notes.append(
401	                    "place: false has no meaning for a new project — the "
402	                        + (result.isVoiceOver ? "voice-over" : "picture") + " IS the "
403	                        + "document, so its clips are on the timeline, one per segment and "
404	                        + "the first at 0.")
405	            }
406	            notes.append(contentsOf: landingNotes)
407	            notes.append(contentsOf: Self.resultNotes(result))
408	            if !notes.isEmpty { fields["note"] = notes.joined(separator: " ") }
409	            fields["ok"] = true
410	            fields["project"] = summary(document)
411	            return (try jsonResult(fields), document)
412	        }
413	    }

415	    /// SERVER THREAD. `land` on main, and in the same hop, when the choice
416	    /// asks for it, Remove Background over the camera clips as its own step
417	    /// (road map creator-jobs CO8, spec §11 CO-81, `camera_cutout` or
418	    /// `camera_cutout_error`); then, when the choice asks for it,
419	    /// Enhance Voice over the recording's voice clips as its own step (spec
420	    /// §11 AU-68 (f)): `decide` polled through `onMain` every
421	    /// `RecordingEnhance.checkInterval`, then `enhance_voice`'s own body at
422	    /// its default target (a tool reads no `UserDefaults`); then, when it asks
423	    /// for any, the polish on landing (road map creator-jobs CU10, spec §11
424	    /// CU-101 (j), `polishLanded`). The answer is `land`'s with `enhance`
425	    /// (that body's answer) or `enhance_error`, the polish's answers or
426	    /// `…_error` sentences, and `project` read again, last, when any ran.
427	    func landAndEnhance(_ result: RecordingResult, place: Bool) throws -> String {
428	        let stop = AgentLane.shared.callCancel
429	        let (answer, document, cutout) = try onMain {
430	            () throws -> (String, ProjectDocument, [UInt32]) in
431	            let (answer, document) = try self.land(result, place: place)
432	            // CO-81: Remove Background, its own step, before Enhance Voice and the polish.
433	            return (answer, document, RecordingCutout.apply(result, in: document))
434	        }
435	        let polish = !RecordingPolish.commands(of: result.choice).isEmpty
436	        let wantsCutout = result.choice.cameraCutout
437	        guard result.choice.enhanceMicrophone || polish || wantsCutout else { return answer }
438	        var fields = Self.resultObject(answer) ?? [:]
439	        if wantsCutout {
440	            if cutout.isEmpty {
441	                fields["camera_cutout_error"] = RecordingCutout.noCameraSentence
442	            } else {
443	                fields["camera_cutout"] = ["clips": cutout]
444	            }
445	        }
446	        if result.choice.enhanceMicrophone {
447	            try enhanceLanded(result, in: document, stop: stop, into: &fields)
448	        }
449	        if polish { polishLanded(result, in: document, into: &fields) }
450	        fields["project"] = onMain { self.summary(document) }

452	    }

454	    /// SERVER THREAD. AU-68 (f)'s wait and Enhance Voice, its answer or
455	    /// `enhance_error` written into `fields`.
456	    private func enhanceLanded(
457	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument, stop: AgentCallCancel?,
458	        into fields: inout [String: Any]
459	    ) throws {
460	        let (clips, scope) = onMain {
461	            (RecordingEnhance.voiceClips(of: result, in: document), document.scope)
462	        }
463	        let started = Date()
464	        var step = RecordingEnhance.Step.wait
465	        while step == .wait, stop?.isCancelled != true {
466	            step = onMain { () -> RecordingEnhance.Step in
467	                let present = RecordingEnhance.present(clips, in: document)
468	                return RecordingEnhance.decide(
469	                    clips: present, analysed: RecordingEnhance.isAnalysed(present, in: document),
470	                    busy: RecordingEnhance.isBusy(document, scope: scope),
471	                    elapsed: Date().timeIntervalSince(started))
472	            }
473	            if step == .wait { Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: RecordingEnhance.checkInterval) }
474	        }
475	        switch step {
476	        case .enhance(let ids):
477	            do {
478	                let enhanced = try enhanceVoice(
479	                    document: document, clips: ids, targetLUFS: AudioNormalize.defaultTargetLUFS)
480	                fields["enhance"] = Self.resultObject(enhanced) ?? enhanced
481	            } catch let error as ToolError {
482	                fields["enhance_error"] = error.message
483	            }
484	        case .drop:
485	            fields["enhance_error"] = RecordingEnhance.noVoiceSentence
486	        case .giveUp:
487	            fields["enhance_error"] = RecordingEnhance.notReadyToolSentence
488	        case .wait:
489	            fields["enhance_error"] =
490	                "record_screen was stopped while the microphone's sound was being analysed, so "
491	                + "Enhance Voice did not run."
492	        }
493	    }

495	    /// The object a `jsonResult` envelope's text holds, nil for anything else.

498	            let call = (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(envelope.utf8)))

500	            let content = call["content"] as? [[String: Any]],
501	            let text = content.first?["text"] as? String
502	        else { return nil }
503	        return (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(text.utf8))) as? [String: Any]
504	    }

635	            return try addShortcutOverlays(

58	        var clip: UInt32?
59	        var micMedia: UInt32?
60	        var micClip: UInt32?
61	        var cameraMedia: UInt32?

71	            self.micClip = micClip

241	    static func resultNotes(_ result: RecordingResult) -> [String] {
242	        [
243	            result.unreadableNote, result.leftOutVoiceNote, microphoneNote(result),
244	            result.camera?.problem, result.camera?.note,
245	            result.cameraSegmentsNote,

247	            result.cursorSegmentsNote,

252	    /// snapshot by path, SEGMENT BY SEGMENT — `untitled(around:)` placed
253	    /// them (the first picture as the document, the rest through
254	    /// `remainderPlacement`), so nothing here predicted an id, and a file
255	    /// the remainder landed as media alone (its sentence in the landing's
256	    /// `notes`) answers a `media` and no `clip`, which is the truth. A new
257	    /// project has no nest, so its top-level clips are the only clips there

261	    ) -> [RecordingSegmentIds] {
262	        let snapshot = document.project.snapshot
263	        return result.segments.map { segment in
264	            let media = landedMedia(for: segment.descriptor.path, in: snapshot)
265	            let micMedia = segment.micDescriptor.flatMap { landedMedia(for: $0.path, in: snapshot) }
266	            let cameraMedia = segment.cameraDescriptor.flatMap {

271	                micMedia: micMedia, micClip: micMedia.flatMap { landedClip(of: $0, in: snapshot) },
272	                cameraMedia: cameraMedia,

278	    /// four lists, the ids it predicted off the purely-applied trial (R1's
279	    /// contract: `next_id` before each op that mints) and the ones the panel
280	    /// selects, so the tool reports what the panel highlights. All four
281	    /// lists have ONE entry per segment, in order, nil where nothing was
282	    /// minted (`Placement`'s doc), so every one is indexed by SEGMENT and

284	    /// `mic…` lists as "segments with a microphone file" were met, and a

286	    /// one. Read BEFORE the commit, as R1 read the singulars, which is what
287	    /// lets `land()` keep `editResult`'s tail.

723	    /// One landing's follow: its document, its clips, the scope it landed in,
724	    /// when, and the timer.
725	    private final class Follow {
726	        weak var document: ProjectDocument?
727	        var clips: [UInt32]
728	        var scope: UInt32?
729	        var started: Date
730	        var timer: Timer?
731	
732	        init(document: ProjectDocument, clips: [UInt32], scope: UInt32?) {
733	            self.document = document
734	            self.clips = clips
735	            self.scope = scope
736	            self.started = Date()

741	    /// twice). A second landing into a document with a follow under way joins

743	    private static var follows: [Int: Follow] = [:]

745	    /// The panel's landing hands its result here once it has committed. A
746	    /// no-op unless the choice asked for it. Main.
747	    static func follow(_ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument) {
748	        guard result.choice.enhanceMicrophone else { return }
749	        let clips = voiceClips(of: result, in: document)
750	        let key = document.recipeKey
751	        if let pending = follows[key] {
752	            pending.clips = Array(Set(pending.clips + clips)).sorted()
753	            pending.scope = document.scope
754	            pending.started = Date()
755	            return
756	        }
757	        let follow = Follow(document: document, clips: clips, scope: document.scope)
758	        follows[key] = follow
759	        // `scheduledTimer` adds it in the DEFAULT mode: it waits out a drag.
760	        follow.timer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: checkInterval, repeats: true) {
761	            [weak document] timer in
762	            guard let document else {
763	                timer.invalidate()
764	                follows[key] = nil
765	                return
766	            }
767	            tick(document)
768	        }

783	    /// (the type doc), then act. Main.

785	        guard let follow = follows[document.recipeKey] else { return }
786	        let clips = present(follow.clips, in: document)
787	        let window = RecorderPanelController.editor(of: document)?.view.window

801	        case .drop, .wait:

856	            case .shortcutOverlays: return "Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays"

865	        case run(Command, [UInt32])

912	    /// Documents whose speech wait has started the cache pass, by `recipeKey` (CU-101 (c)).
913	    private static var cachesStarted: Set<Int> = []

915	    /// CU-101 (c). Auto Zoom and Add Shortcut Overlays need only the cursor files, which the
916	    /// caller has read. The speed-up is ready unless `SpeedUpTyping.resolve` answers `.waiting`;
917	    /// its first `.waiting` for the document starts `generateCaches()` (a pass that could not
918	    /// read a file is not retried until the next open). A throw counts as ready, so the run
919	    /// reports the refusal. Main.
920	    static func isReady(
921	        _ command: Command, clips: [UInt32], tracks: [UInt32: ReelCursor],
922	        speedUp: SpeedUpTypingSettings, in document: ProjectDocument
923	    ) -> Bool {
924	        guard command == .speedUpTyping else { return true }
925	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
926	        let outcome: SpeedUpTypingOutcome
927	        do {
928	            outcome = try SpeedUpTyping.resolve(
929	                clips.compactMap { snapshot.clip($0) }, tracks: tracks,
930	                project: document.editedProject, cacheDirectory: document.cacheDirectory,
931	                settings: speedUp, from: nil, to: nil)
932	        } catch {
933	            return true
934	        }
935	        guard case .waiting = outcome else {
936	            cachesStarted.remove(document.recipeKey)
937	            return true
938	        }
939	        if cachesStarted.insert(document.recipeKey).inserted { document.generateCaches() }
940	        return false
941	    }
942	
943	    /// The wait for `document` is over: a later wait starts the pass again. Main.
944	    static func forgetWait(_ document: ProjectDocument) {
945	        cachesStarted.remove(document.recipeKey)
946	    }

948	    /// CU-101 (e), in this order. Pure.
949	    static func decide(
950	        command: Command, clips: [UInt32], enhancing: Bool, ready: Bool, busy: Bool,
951	        elapsed: TimeInterval
952	    ) -> Step {
953	        if clips.isEmpty { return .drop }
954	        if enhancing { return .wait }
955	        if ready && !busy { return .run(command, clips) }
956	        if elapsed >= waitLimit { return .giveUp(command) }
957	        return .wait
958	    }

64	struct RecordingLanding {
65	    enum Target {
66	        case document(ProjectDocument)
67	        case newProject
68	    }
69	
70	    /// The undo step's name, for both doors — the whole landing, every
71	    /// picture and every microphone in one list.
72	    static let actionName = "Add Recording"
73	
74	    // MARK: - Where
75	
76	    /// The document a `.document(recipeKey:)` destination names, looked up
77	    /// among the open documents by `recipeKey` — minted by
78	    /// `RecipeSource.register()`, monotonic and never reused, so a document
79	    /// that closed mid-recording is a lookup that fails and not a dangling
80	    /// pointer or (the `ObjectIdentifier` trap `RelinkSheetController`
81	    /// records) the next document allocated at the same address. A miss, and
82	    /// `.newProject`, both answer `.newProject`. Main thread.
83	    static func resolve(_ destination: RecordingDestination) -> Target {
84	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
85	        guard case .document(let key) = destination else { return .newProject }
86	        let open = NSDocumentController.shared.documents.compactMap { $0 as? ProjectDocument }
87	        guard let document = open.first(where: { $0.recipeKey == key }) else {
88	            return .newProject
89	        }
90	        return .document(document)
91	    }

93	    // MARK: - What
94	
95	    /// PURE: the op list and the predicted ids for landing `result` in
96	    /// `document` at its playhead, in the container it has open — every
97	    /// segment, as ONE grouped edit.
98	    ///
99	    /// Each segment's picture media goes in first, in order, applied purely
100	    /// against the DOCUMENT's handle (`add_media` is document-level,
101	    /// `ReelOp.documentLevelNames`) and its id read off the result; then,
102	    /// with `place`, the pictures as a sequence on ONE track by the two-try
103	    /// track rule — all of them on the front track of the open container if
104	    /// the core accepts every one there, else all on a new track in front of
105	    /// everything (`addSequence`). The rule is `addGeneratedClip`'s
106	    /// (`EditorViewController+AddClips.swift`) but it cannot be that method:
107	    /// its probe runs against a project that does not hold the media yet,
108	    /// and `add_clip` naming an absent media is an `Err` — every recording
109	    /// would fall to the new-track branch, and the branch would then name
110	    /// the TRACK by the id `add_media` had consumed. `placeImageBackground`
111	    /// / `backgroundMedia(for:in:)` are the precedent: the probe runs over a
112	    /// project that already HOLDS the media.
113	    ///
114	    /// With microphone files the second half — each one's media, ONE new
115	    /// BACK track named "Microphone", each one's clip — is derived from the
116	    /// pictures' purely-applied result, never from one `next_id` read,
117	    /// because the pictures mint `n` or `n + 1` ids and which depends on the
118	    /// branch the track rule took. `place == false` lands every media (the
119	    /// microphones' included) with no clip at all.
120	    ///
121	    /// **A camera beside the screen** (spec §11 CAM-10) lands between the
122	    /// two: each segment's `(Camera).mov` as media, then — with `place` —
123	    /// ONE new FRONT track named "Camera" and each camera clip at its screen
124	    /// segment's start plus its `cameraOffset`, laid out (`addCameras`).
125	    /// The pictures → cameras → microphones order is the one grouped edit's.
126	    ///
127	    /// **A left-out segment's readable voice** (#181 item 2, spec §11
128	    /// recording) is a stretch of its own (`RecordingResult.stretches`): on
129	    /// the picture side a GAP of its slot's length (`pictureStretches`), so
130	    /// the pictures after it start at the slot's end, and on the microphone
131	    /// side a voice at offset 0 at the slot's start, by the same floor rule
132	    /// (`voices(of:)`); `split` reads the answers back per segment and per
133	    /// left-out segment. With no left-out voice the list is the segments.
134	    ///
135	    /// The playhead is nest-local while a nest is open, the ops are unscoped,
136	    /// and the trial stamps the document's scope on the container ops exactly
137	    /// as the commit will. Two refusals are thrown by name rather than
138	    /// answered with a list that would beep: a live gesture (the caller
139	    /// retries when it ends, rather than committing over the gesture's base
140	    /// handle) and anything the core refuses, with the core's own sentence.
141	    ///
142	    /// **The trial sees everything the commit will, the caps included.**
143	    /// Each scoped op is applied to the PARENT handle —
144	    /// `trial.applying(op.scoped(scope))` IS the scoped apply, not a view of
145	    /// it — so `check_caps` and `check_nesting`, which phase 9 runs once on
146	    /// the MERGED parent (`core/src/scope.rs`, `Project::finish`), refuse
147	    /// here with the core's own sentence exactly as they would at the
148	    /// commit: a document at `MAX_TRACKS` throws "too many tracks" before
149	    /// any list is answered, inside a nest or out of one
150	    /// (`tools/proof/recording_probe.py`, section 4, row 8).
151	    ///
152	    /// **One list, one limit.** The pictures and the microphones are ONE
153	    /// grouped edit, so a microphone pair the core refuses takes every
154	    /// picture down with it. The case that reaches it: a document at
155	    /// `MAX_TRACKS` with an empty front track takes the pictures alone (no
156	    /// track is added) and lands NOTHING once a microphone needs its own
157	    /// track. Kept on purpose — half a recording landed, with the voice
158	    /// missing and no undo step that says so, is worse than a refusal — and
159	    /// both doors name the FILES in the refusal, which are on disk whatever
160	    /// happened after them. What is NOT a refusal is a file the core cannot
161	    /// make a clip of at all: it lands as media, with a sentence in `notes`.
162	    static func placement(
163	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument, place: Bool
164	    ) throws -> Placement {
165	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
166	        guard !document.isLiveEditing else {
167	            throw ReelCoreError(
168	                message: "A drag is in progress; the recording can be added when it ends.")
169	        }
170	        if result.isVoiceOver { return try voiceOverPlacement(result, in: document, place: place) }
171	        let scope = document.scope
172	        var trial = document.project
173	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
174	        var notes: [String] = []
175	
176	        var mediaIds: [UInt32] = []
177	        for segment in result.segments {
178	            mediaIds.append(try addMedia(segment.descriptor, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
179	        }
180	        var pictures: [Landed] = []
181	        if place {
182	            let stretches = try pictureStretches(
183	                of: result, mediaIds: mediaIds, in: trial, scope: scope)
184	            pictures = try addSequence(
185	                stretches, from: document.playhead, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops,
186	                notes: &notes)
187	            try addRipples(
188	                pictures.compactMap { $0.clip?.id }, of: result, scope: scope, to: &trial,
189	                ops: &ops)
190	        }
191	        let cameras = try addCameras(
192	            result, screenStarts: place ? segmentStarts(pictures.map { $0.at }, of: result) : nil,
193	            screenClips: split(pictures.map { $0.clip?.id }, of: result).segments,
194	            scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
195	        let microphones = try addMicrophones(
196	            voices(of: result), pictureStarts: place ? pictures.map { $0.at } : nil,
197	            scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
198	        let micMedia = split(microphones.media, of: result)
199	        let micClips = split(microphones.clips, of: result)
200	        return Placement(
201	            ops: ops, mediaIds: mediaIds,
202	            clipIds: place
203	                ? split(pictures.map { $0.clip?.id }, of: result).segments
204	                : mediaIds.map { _ in nil },
205	            micMediaIds: micMedia.segments, micClipIds: micClips.segments, notes: notes,
206	            leftOutMicMediaIds: micMedia.leftOut, leftOutMicClipIds: micClips.leftOut,
207	            cameraMediaIds: cameras.media, cameraClipIds: cameras.clips)
208	    }

210	    // MARK: - The steps, each applied purely and read back
211	
212	    /// `add_media` applied purely; the id it minted, read off the result. A
213	    /// path already in the list is the documented IDENTITY
214	    /// (`core/src/edit_track.rs`), not a failure, and then the id is the
215	    /// entry's, matched by the TRIMMED path because that is what the core
216	    /// stored — `backgroundMedia(for:in:)`'s rule. The op stays in the list
217	    /// either way: `applying(_ ops:)` runs every later op after an identity,
218	    /// so one shape serves both cases and the undo step is one.
219	    static func addMedia(
220	        _ descriptor: MediaDescriptor, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
221	    ) throws -> UInt32 {
222	        let op = ReelOp.addMedia(descriptor: descriptor)
223	        ops.append(op)
224	        if let added = try trial.applying(op).project {
225	            trial = added
226	            guard let id = added.snapshot.media.last?.id else {
227	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(descriptor.path) was added and is not listed.")
228	            }
229	            return id
230	        }
231	        let path = trimmed(descriptor.path)
232	        guard let id = trial.snapshot.media.first(where: { $0.path == path })?.id else {
233	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(path) could not be added to the media list.")
234	        }
235	        return id
236	    }

238	    /// The two-try track rule over a SEQUENCE, for a `trial` that holds
239	    /// every `media`: all of them back to back on the front track of the
240	    /// open container, from `at`; if any one REFUSES there — the overlap
241	    /// rule is the only reason the core has — ALL of them on a new track in
242	    /// front of everything, from the same `at`. The sequence never splits: a
243	    /// recording whose first segment sits on one track and whose second on
244	    /// another would read as two recordings, so a refusal part-way discards
245	    /// the front track's half-placed trial whole (it was a copy) and starts
246	    /// the new track's from the trial that holds the media and no clip. The
247	    /// new track's id is `next_id` off the trial, and each clip's is
248	    /// `next_id` off the trial before its own `add_clip`.
249	    ///
250	    /// Only a REFUSAL (nil) falls through to the new track. An `Err` from
251	    /// the first attempt propagates: the caps are the same on either track,
252	    /// so a `try?` here — R1's shape — turned "too many clips" on a full
253	    /// document into a second attempt that added a track and then reported
254	    /// "too many tracks", the wrong cap, when the document was at both.
255	    /// `notes` takes the winning attempt's sentences (the same either way —
256	    /// a picture too short for a frame is too short on any track). The
257	    /// sequence is the whole stretch list, a left-out voice's gap included,
258	    /// so the rule sees every picture where it will land.
259	    private static func addSequence(
260	        _ stretches: [PictureStretch], from at: Ticks, scope: UInt32?,
261	        to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp], notes: inout [String]
262	    ) throws -> [Landed] {
263	        let container = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot
264	        if let front = container.tracks.last?.id {
265	            var attempt = trial
266	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
267	            var attemptNotes: [String] = []
268	            if let placed = try placeBackToBack(
269	                stretches, on: front, from: at, scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps,
270	                notes: &attemptNotes)
271	            {
272	                trial = attempt
273	                ops += attemptOps
274	                notes += attemptNotes
275	                return placed
276	            }
277	        }
278	        // Index 0 is the BACK of the stack (§6), so the count is the front.
279	        let addTrack = ReelOp.addTrack(index: container.tracks.count)
280	        let track = trial.snapshot.nextId
281	        guard let withTrack = try trial.applying(addTrack.scoped(scope)).project else {
282	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "A track for the recording could not be added.")
283	        }
284	        var attempt = withTrack
285	        var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = [addTrack]
286	        var attemptNotes: [String] = []
287	        guard
288	            let placed = try placeBackToBack(
289	                stretches, on: track, from: at, scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps,
290	                notes: &attemptNotes)
291	        else {
292	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "The recording could not be placed on a new track.")
293	        }
294	        trial = attempt
295	        ops += attemptOps
296	        notes += attemptNotes
297	        return placed
298	    }

300	    /// The clip `id` as the core reports it, read off the CONTAINER the ops
301	    /// are measured against — the nest's view while a scope is open, since
302	    /// a nested clip is not in the parent's `clips`. An id the trial does
303	    /// not list after its own `add_clip` accepted it is a throw, not a
304	    /// guess.
305	    static func clip(_ id: UInt32, in trial: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?) throws -> ClipSnapshot {
306	        let container = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot
307	        guard let clip = container.clips.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else {
308	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "Clip \(id) was placed and is not listed.")
309	        }
310	        return clip
311	    }

313	    /// The container the clip ops are measured against: the nest's view
314	    /// while a scope is open (its tracks and clips at the top level, its
315	    /// `next_id` the parent's), else the trial itself. A scope naming a nest
316	    /// the trial has not got is a refusal, not a fallback — `clampViewState`
317	    /// clears one before anything reads it, so this arm is a race with an
318	    /// undo and the caller should not land on the timeline by accident.
319	    static func view(of trial: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?) throws -> ReelProject {

474	    /// sequence had reached, and the next picture starts the gap's length
475	    /// later. Answers one `Landed` per stretch, in order.

477	        _ stretches: [PictureStretch], on track: UInt32, from at: Ticks, scope: UInt32?,
478	        to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp], notes: inout [String]
479	    ) throws -> [Landed]? {

513	    /// two grid points, which is not one — so a landing under the floor is
514	    /// discarded whole and the add is made again at `floor` plus a frame,
515	    /// whose nearest frame is at or above the floor and within a frame of
516	    /// it. What comes back therefore satisfies `floor ≤ start ≤ at + frame`:
517	    /// touching, or a sub-frame gap at an inexact rate, never an overlap

519	    /// outside that band after the second try is a throw, not a guess. nil
520	    /// is the core's refusal — an overlap the rule will not accept — and
521	    /// the op is appended and the trial advanced only for the clip returned.
522	    static func placeClip(
523	        _ media: UInt32, on track: UInt32, at: Ticks, notBelow floor: Ticks, scope: UInt32?,

525	    ) throws -> ClipSnapshot? {
526	        precondition(at >= floor, "a clip is asked for at or above its floor")
527	        let frame = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas.fps.frameDuration
528	        for requested in [at, floor + frame] {
529	            let op = ReelOp.addClip(track: track, media: media, at: requested)
530	            let id = trial.snapshot.nextId

533	            if landed.start < floor { continue }
534	            guard landed.start <= at + frame else {
535	                throw ReelCoreError(
536	                    message: "Clip \(id) landed at \(landed.start), more than a frame past \(at).")

538	            trial = next
539	            ops.append(op)
540	            return landed
541	        }

544	    }

625	    /// 0. With several, two voices on one track can neither overlap — a
626	    /// refusal, or worse a sub-frame overlap the rule ACCEPTS as a
627	    /// transition, minting a cross dissolve between two halves of one
628	    /// recording — nor be placed late (the same wrong sound as R1's negative
629	    /// start put at 0), so the floor for voice `k` is the previous voice's

632	    /// end is on the frame grid because the core snapped its start and its

647	            pictureStarts.map { $0.count == voices.count } ?? true,

650	        for voice in voices {
651	            if let mic = voice.descriptor {
652	                media.append(try addMedia(mic, to: &trial, ops: &ops))

654	                media.append(nil)

656	        }

663	            guard let id = media[k], let start = starts[k] else {
664	                clips.append(nil)

666	            }
667	            var attempt = trial
668	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []

671	                on = added
672	            } else {

699	    /// One voice's clip on `track`, at `pictureAt − offset` and never below
700	    /// `floor` — 0 for the first voice, the previous voice's end after it.
701	    /// nil, with a sentence in `notes`, for a voice that gets no clip; the
702	    /// trial and the ops are advanced only for a clip returned.
703	    ///
704	    /// **The sign.** `offset` is the screen's did-start minus the
705	    /// microphone's, in ticks; positive means the picture began AFTER the
706	    /// microphone, so the microphone's content LEADS and its clip starts
707	    /// that much earlier than the picture's. R0 measured it centred near
708	    /// zero with a 35 ms scatter (road map 3, R0 q6b) and a different number
709	    /// at every resume (q7), and the landing applies each segment's measured
710	    /// number — never a constant, never the first segment's.
711	    ///
712	    /// **When that start is below the floor** — the picture at 0 with the
713	    /// microphone ahead of it, or a later voice whose picture began less
714	    /// than its offset after the previous voice ended — the clip cannot
715	    /// start there: below 0 there is no timeline, below the previous voice's
716	    /// end there is a clip, and placing it AT the floor would leave the
717	    /// voice LATE by the difference. So the head is trimmed off instead, and
718	    /// it stays one grouped edit: `add_clip` at the floor, `trim_start` to
719	    /// the landed start + head (the core sets the start there and advances
720	    /// `in` by the same amount — `core/src/edit_clip.rs`), `move_clip` back
721	    /// by what the trim advanced, read off the trimmed clip (the head, at
722	    /// an exact rate; at an inexact one the grid point nearest it). A
723	    /// `slip` would be the one-op spelling and cannot be used: the clip
724	    /// covers its whole media, so the slip's clamp reduces it to nothing.
725	    /// The head is the core's own snap of the shortfall
726	    /// (`ReelTime.snapToFrame`, the rounding every time argument gets), so a
727	    /// start within half a frame of the floor makes no trim and the two ops
728	    /// are not sent — the core's snap of that start lands it on the floor —
729	    /// while a start further below is trimmed rather than left to the snap,
730	    /// because the core would snap it to the frame BELOW the floor: at 0
731	    /// clamped up and late by a frame, above 0 a one-frame overlap the rule
732	    /// accepts as a transition. Limit: the grid is the picture's frame — at
733	    /// 60 fps 16.7 ms — so the alignment is exact to half a frame and no
734	    /// finer.
735	    ///
736	    /// **Every step is read back, and two things are decided by what comes
737	    /// back** (the R2 review). `trim_start` clamps its `to` at a frame
738	    /// before the clip's end, so a voice no longer than its head — an 80 ms
739	    /// file whose picture began 100 ms after it — used to be trimmed to a
740	    /// one-frame sliver and then moved back INTO the previous voice, which
741	    /// `move_clips` refused: `applying(_ ops:)` still answered non-nil (the
742	    /// add and the trim had changed something), the trial "succeeded", and
743	    /// the commit ran a refused op inside its undo step with the sliver
744	    /// sitting late. Now the trimmed clip's start is compared with the
745	    /// core's own snap of the requested `to`, and a start that is not it is
746	    /// the clamp: the voice is wholly under its head, mints NO clip, and its
747	    /// sentence names the file. And the moved clip must land exactly where
748	    /// the core's snap of the delta says, at or above the floor, or the
749	    /// throw names the file — a refused op can never ride a committed list.
750	    /// At an INEXACT rate the move's landing can be a tick under a floor
751	    /// that is a grid point (the delta and the trim round separately; grid
752	    /// points are not closed under addition), which the rule would accept
753	    /// and dress as a transition, so that one case is done once more a
754	    /// frame up with a frame more head: the content stays aligned to the
755	    /// tick, the voice starts a sub-frame gap after the previous one, and
756	    /// its first frame past the head is the price — the documented limit of
757	    /// such a rate, beside the pictures' own sub-frame gap.
758	    static func addMicrophoneClip(
759	        _ media: UInt32, on track: UInt32, pictureAt: Ticks, offset: Ticks, floor: Ticks,
760	        scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp], notes: inout [String]
761	    ) throws -> ClipSnapshot? {
762	        let file = try mediaEntry(media, in: trial, scope: scope)
763	        let fps = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas.fps
764	        if let note = tooShortNote(file, at: fps) {
765	            notes.append(note)

767	        }
768	        let start = pictureAt - offset
769	        let head = start < floor ? ReelTime.snapToFrame(floor - start, fps: fps) : 0

771	            guard
772	                let placed = try placeClip(
773	                    media, on: track, at: max(start, floor), notBelow: floor, scope: scope,
774	                    to: &trial, ops: &ops)

776	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(file.path) could not be placed on its track.")
777	            }
