779	        }
780	        let frame = fps.frameDuration
781	        for (at, head) in [(floor, head), (floor + frame, head + frame)] {
782	            var attempt = trial
783	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
784	            guard
785	                let placed = try headTrimmed(
786	                    media, file: file, on: track, at: at, head: head, floor: floor, fps: fps,
787	                    scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps)
788	            else {
789	                notes.append(underNote(file, head: head, floor: floor))
790	                return nil
791	            }
792	            if placed.start >= floor {
793	                trial = attempt
794	                ops += attemptOps
795	                return placed
796	            }
797	        }
798	        throw ReelCoreError(
799	            message: "\(file.path) could not be placed clear of the previous microphone clip.")
800	    }
801	
802	    /// The dance once, on `trial`: the add at `at` (never under `floor`),
803	    /// the trim to the landed start + `head`, the move back by what the trim
804	    /// advanced. nil when the trim clamped — the voice is wholly under its
805	    /// head — with the trial left as it was; every other surprise is a
806	    /// throw naming the file. The clip returned may still sit a tick under
807	    /// the floor at an inexact rate, which the caller reads.
808	    static func headTrimmed(
809	        _ media: UInt32, file: MediaSnapshot, on track: UInt32, at: Ticks, head: Ticks,
810	        floor: Ticks, fps: Fps, scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
811	    ) throws -> ClipSnapshot? {
812	        guard
813	            let added = try placeClip(
814	                media, on: track, at: at, notBelow: floor, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops)
815	        else {
816	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(file.path) could not be placed on its track.")
817	        }
818	        let trim = ReelOp.trimStart(clip: added.id, to: added.start + head)
819	        let promisedTrim = ReelTime.snapToFrame(added.start + head, fps: fps)
820	        guard let trimmed = try trial.applying(trim.scoped(scope)).project,
821	            try clip(added.id, in: trimmed, scope: scope).start == promisedTrim
822	        else { return nil }
823	        let advanced = promisedTrim - added.start
824	        let move = ReelOp.moveClip(clips: [added.id], delta: -advanced)
825	        let promisedStart = promisedTrim + ReelTime.snapToFrame(-advanced, fps: fps)
826	        guard let moved = try trimmed.applying(move.scoped(scope)).project else {
827	            throw ReelCoreError(
828	                message: "\(file.path) could not be moved back by its \(milliseconds(advanced)) ms head.")
829	        }
830	        let landed = try clip(added.id, in: moved, scope: scope)
831	        guard landed.start == promisedStart, landed.source.sourceIn == advanced else {
832	            throw ReelCoreError(
833	                message: "\(file.path) landed at \(landed.start) with \(landed.source.sourceIn) "
834	                    + "trimmed, not at \(promisedStart) with \(advanced).")
835	        }
836	        trial = moved
837	        ops += [trim, move]
838	        return landed
839	    }
840	
841	    /// The sentence for a voice wholly under its head.
842	    private static func underNote(_ file: MediaSnapshot, head: Ticks, floor: Ticks) -> String {
843	        let clear = floor == 0 ? "the start of the timeline" : "the previous microphone clip"
844	        return "\(file.path) was added to the media list without a clip: less than a frame of "
845	            + "it would remain after the \(milliseconds(head)) ms head that keeps it clear of "
846	            + "\(clear)."
847	    }
848	}
849	// app/Sources/RecordingLanding+VoiceOver.swift — where a finished VOICE-OVER
850	// goes (spec §11 recording, "A voice-over is a recording with no picture",
851	// #99).
852	//
853	// A voice-over is an ordinary `RecordingResult` whose every segment's
854	// `descriptor` is an `.m4a` (`isVoiceOver`). `placement(_:in:place:)` forwards
855	// it here after its live-edit guard, and the rule is not the picture rule:
856	// every file lands on ONE new BACK track named "Microphone" — where a screen
857	// recording's microphone lands — touching, from the playhead, in the one
858	// grouped edit both doors commit as "Add Recording". Never the front track,
859	// and never an existing Microphone track: no rule says which track is "the"
860	// voice track. The placing is `placeBackToBack`'s (`+Placing`), so every clip
861	// is read back and a file under a frame lands as media with its
862	// `tooShortNote`; the track is kept only when at least one clip landed on it.
863	//
864	// A NEW project needs nothing here: `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)` makes
865	// the first file the document (audio-only, 1920×1080 at the chosen rate) and
866	// `remainderPlacement` puts the later files touching it on its one track.
867	
868	import AppKit
869	
870	extension RecordingLanding {
871	    /// PURE, main thread: the voice-over's ops and predicted ids. Every
872	    /// file's `add_media` in order (document-level, unscoped); then, with
873	    /// `place`, on a trial copy, `add_track` at index 0 named
874	    /// `microphoneTrackName` and every file back to back from the playhead
875	    /// on it. A refusal on that new, empty track is thrown by name. The
876	    /// track and its clips are kept only when at least one clip landed —
877	    /// every file under a frame adds media and notes alone, and then no
878	    /// `add_track` is even tried, so a document at the track cap does not
879	    /// throw for a track nothing would land on. `clipIds` has
880	    /// one entry per segment; the two `mic…` lists are all nil (a
881	    /// voice-over's voice IS its descriptor); the two left-out lists have
882	    /// one nil per `unreadable` entry. The ops come back unscoped, the
883	    /// container ops stamped by the caller's door as for any landing.
884	    static func voiceOverPlacement(
885	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument, place: Bool
886	    ) throws -> Placement {
887	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
888	        let scope = document.scope
889	        var trial = document.project
890	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
891	        var notes: [String] = []
892	        var mediaIds: [UInt32] = []
893	        for segment in result.segments {
894	            mediaIds.append(try addMedia(segment.descriptor, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
895	        }
896	        var clipIds: [UInt32?] = mediaIds.map { _ in nil }
897	        let fps = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas.fps
898	        let shortNotes = try mediaIds.map {
899	            tooShortNote(try mediaEntry($0, in: trial, scope: scope), at: fps)
900	        }
901	        let canLand = shortNotes.contains { $0 == nil }
902	        if place && !canLand {
903	            notes += shortNotes.compactMap { $0 }
904	        } else if place {
905	            var attempt = trial
906	            let track = attempt.snapshot.nextId
907	            let addTrack = ReelOp.addTrack(index: 0, name: microphoneTrackName)
908	            guard let withTrack = try attempt.applying(addTrack.scoped(scope)).project else {
909	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "A track for the voice-over could not be added.")
910	            }
911	            attempt = withTrack
912	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = [addTrack]
913	            guard
914	                let placed = try placeBackToBack(
915	                    mediaIds.map { PictureStretch.picture($0) }, on: track,
916	                    from: document.playhead, scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps,
917	                    notes: &notes)
918	            else {
919	                throw ReelCoreError(
920	                    message: "The voice-over could not be placed on its new Microphone track.")
921	            }
922	            if placed.contains(where: { $0.clip != nil }) {
923	                trial = attempt
924	                ops += attemptOps
925	                clipIds = placed.map { $0.clip?.id }
926	            }
927	        }
928	        let none: [UInt32?] = mediaIds.map { _ in nil }
929	        let leftOut: [UInt32?] = result.unreadable.map { _ in nil }
930	        return Placement(
931	            ops: ops, mediaIds: mediaIds, clipIds: clipIds, micMediaIds: none, micClipIds: none,
932	            notes: notes, leftOutMicMediaIds: leftOut, leftOutMicClipIds: leftOut)
933	    }
934	}

965	    /// The same step's name when the remainder holds more than a voice — a
966	    /// paused recording's later segments, with or without microphones.

968	    /// segment is the document and stays under the undo; what the step takes

990	        if result.segments.count == 1 {
991	            let voice =
992	                result.segments[0].micDescriptor != nil
993	                || result.unreadable.contains(where: { $0.micDescriptor != nil })
994	            if result.segments[0].cameraDescriptor != nil {
995	                return voice ? cameraMicrophoneActionName : cameraActionName

997	            if voice { return microphoneActionName }

1000	        return segmentsActionName

1003	    /// Everything a fresh untitled document does NOT already hold, for
1004	    /// `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`, whose `makeProject` placed the
1005	    /// FIRST segment's picture at 0 on track 1 before anything else could
1006	    /// run: segments 2…n's media and their pictures on that same track from
1007	    /// clip 1's end, then every segment's microphone by the floor rule. nil
1008	    /// when there is nothing to add — one segment, no microphone, no camera
1009	    /// and no ripples (`wantsRipples` with a cursor not in the picture, CU-31).
1010	    /// `placement(_:in:place:)` cannot serve it — the first picture's
1011	    /// `add_media` would be the documented identity and its `add_clip` at 0
1012	    /// would meet its own clip on the front track, refuse, and put the whole
1013	    /// sequence a SECOND time on a new track. The answer reads as a whole
1014	    /// landing: `mediaIds[0]` and `clipIds[0]` name the picture the document
1015	    /// holds.
1016	    ///
1017	    /// Clip 1 is the FIRST clip whose source is the first segment's media,
1018	    /// and the later pictures go on ITS track from ITS end — read off the
1019	    /// document, not assumed to be track 1 at 0. That is exact for the one
1020	    /// caller: `makeProject` places exactly one clip. A document holding the
1021	    /// same media in several clips has no single answer here, and this
1022	    /// method does not pretend to one — it is `untitled(around:)`'s, not a
1023	    /// general "add the rest of a recording to a document" op. The later
1024	    /// pictures take no two-try rule: a refusal on a fresh document's one
1025	    /// track is not a track choice to fall back from but something wrong
1026	    /// with a file, and is thrown by name.
1027	    ///
1028	    /// **Without clip 1** — `makeProject` tolerates a first picture the core
1029	    /// refuses (a media with no duration) and opens the file in the Media
1030	    /// tab — nothing on the timeline says where the recording is, so the
1031	    /// remainder lands as MEDIA ONLY, `place: false`'s shape, with a
1032	    /// sentence per file in `notes`. The first shape here placed every
1033	    /// voice against a picture at 0, R1's one-segment fallback, which with
1034	    /// several voices stacked each one under the last (the floor rule
1035	    /// trimming a whole voice off) — a wrong sound where a Media-tab list
1036	    /// is at least an honest one.
1037	    ///
1038	    /// **A left-out segment's readable voice** (#181 item 2) is a stretch:
1039	    /// after clip 1 a gap the later pictures skip and a voice at its start;
1040	    /// BEFORE clip 1, which is the document at 0, media only with
1041	    /// `leadingVoiceNote`; without clip 1, media only with `unplacedNote`.
1042	    ///
1043	    /// **A camera beside the screen** (spec §11 CAM-10 (4)) lands after the
1044	    /// later pictures and before the voices, by `addCameras` against each
1045	    /// segment's picture start — clip 1's included — on ONE new track in
1046	    /// front of the pictures', laid out with its segment's picture; without
1047	    /// clip 1, as media only with
1048	    /// `unplacedNote`.
1049	    ///
1050	    /// **The ripples** (CU-31 (c)) go on clip 1 and the later pictures right
1051	    /// after those are placed (`addRipples`); without clip 1 there are none.
1052	    static func remainderPlacement(
1053	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument
1054	    ) throws -> Placement? {
1055	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
1056	        let hasMicrophone = result.segments.contains { $0.micDescriptor != nil }
1057	        let hasLeftOutVoice = result.unreadable.contains { $0.micDescriptor != nil }
1058	        let hasCamera = result.segments.contains { $0.cameraDescriptor != nil }
1059	        let more = result.segments.count > 1 || hasMicrophone || hasLeftOutVoice || hasCamera
1060	        guard more || wantsRipples(result) else { return nil }
1061	        let path = trimmed(result.descriptor.path)
1062	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
1063	        guard let mediaId = snapshot.media.first(where: { $0.path == path })?.id else {
1064	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(path) is not in the document's media list.")
1065	        }
1066	        let first = snapshot.clips.first { clip in
1067	            if case .media(let id, _, _) = clip.source { return id == mediaId }
1068	            return false
1069	        }
1070	        let scope = document.scope
1071	        var trial = document.project
1072	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
1073	        var notes: [String] = []
1074	        var mediaIds = [mediaId]
1075	        for segment in result.segments.dropFirst() {
1076	            mediaIds.append(try addMedia(segment.descriptor, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
1077	        }
1078	        var starts: [Ticks?]?
1079	        var clips: [UInt32?] = result.stretches.map { _ in nil }
1080	        if let first = first {
1081	            let placed = try remainderStretches(
1082	                result, after: first, mediaIds: mediaIds, firstPath: path, scope: scope,
1083	                to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
1084	            starts = placed.starts
1085	            clips = placed.clips
1086	            try addRipples(
1087	                clips.compactMap { $0 }, of: result, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops)
1088	        } else {
1089	            for segment in result.segments.dropFirst() {
1090	                notes.append(unplacedNote(segment.descriptor.path, behind: path))
1091	            }
1092	            for segment in result.segments {
1093	                if let camera = segment.cameraDescriptor {
1094	                    notes.append(unplacedNote(camera.path, behind: path))
1095	                }
1096	            }
1097	            for segment in result.segments {
1098	                if let mic = segment.micDescriptor { notes.append(unplacedNote(mic.path, behind: path)) }
1099	            }
1100	            for left in result.unreadable {
1101	                if let mic = left.micDescriptor { notes.append(unplacedNote(mic.path, behind: path)) }
1102	            }
1103	        }
1104	        let cameras = try addCameras(
1105	            result, screenStarts: starts.map { segmentStarts($0, of: result) },
1106	            screenClips: split(clips, of: result).segments, scope: scope,
1107	            to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)

1109	            voices(of: result), pictureStarts: starts,
1110	            scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)

1112	        guard more || !ops.isEmpty else { return nil }

1114	        let micClips = split(microphones.clips, of: result)

1116	            ops: ops, mediaIds: mediaIds, clipIds: split(clips, of: result).segments,
1117	            micMediaIds: micMedia.segments, micClipIds: micClips.segments, notes: notes,
1118	            leftOutMicMediaIds: micMedia.leftOut, leftOutMicClipIds: micClips.leftOut,
1119	            cameraMediaIds: cameras.media, cameraClipIds: cameras.clips)

30	/// placement's four lists, each indexed by SEGMENT — one entry per segment
31	/// since the R2 review, nil where nothing was minted — the ids it predicted
32	/// and the panel selects), so `recordingFields` derives the top-level four
33	/// from the first entry and no caller writes an id key by hand. Each entry
34	/// of `segments` also carries its own `width`, `height` and `fps`, because
35	/// on a variable-rate file `fps` genuinely differs from segment to segment.
36	///
37	/// **A failure after the recording was written names the file** (R1 review):
38	/// the recorder's own `.filesKept` already does that for a failure INSIDE
39	/// the recorder, and `savedButNotAdded` is the same rule for the three
40	/// places the TOOL can fail after a clean result — the placement's trial,
41	/// the commit, and the untitled document — because a caller told only "a
42	/// drag is in progress" has no way to find the footage that exists. The
43	/// files are spelled by `RecordingResult.filesClause`, the ONE spelling the
44	/// panel's note shares: every movie comma-joined, then every microphone file
45	/// that landed; the one-segment sentence is byte for byte R1's.
46	extension AgentServer {
47	
48	    // MARK: - The result
49	
50	    /// The ids ONE segment's files landed as, each nil until known: a
51	    /// `place: false` landing mints no clip, a segment whose microphone
52	    /// failed has no `micMedia`, and a result built before any landing
53	    /// (a probe's, or a throw's) has none of the four. `cameraMedia` and
54	    /// `cameraClip` are a camera beside the screen's (spec §11 CAM-10 (6)),
55	    /// written per segment only, never at the top level.
56	    struct RecordingSegmentIds {
57	        var media: UInt32?
58	        var clip: UInt32?
59	        var micMedia: UInt32?
60	        var micClip: UInt32?
61	        var cameraMedia: UInt32?
62	        var cameraClip: UInt32?
63	
64	        init(
65	            media: UInt32? = nil, clip: UInt32? = nil, micMedia: UInt32? = nil,
66	            micClip: UInt32? = nil, cameraMedia: UInt32? = nil, cameraClip: UInt32? = nil
67	        ) {
68	            self.media = media
69	            self.clip = clip
70	            self.micMedia = micMedia
71	            self.micClip = micClip
72	            self.cameraMedia = cameraMedia
73	            self.cameraClip = cameraClip
74	        }
75	    }
76	
77	    /// What the files are, and — through `ids`, one entry per segment in
78	    /// order, absent entries reading as unknown — where they landed. The
79	    /// top-level keys are the FIRST segment's: `path`, `width`, `height`,
80	    /// `fps`, `has_audio`, `audio_tracks` (what the MOVIE holds, 1 with
81	    /// system audio, else 0: the microphone is a second file, reported as
82	    /// `mic_path` and `mic_duration`, never a second track of this one),
83	    /// `mic_offset` — ALWAYS present, 0 for a segment with no microphone,
84	    /// because the key is a measurement and not a flag: `mic_path` is what
85	    /// says whether a file landed — and `media` / `clip` / `mic_media` /
86	    /// `mic_clip` from `ids.first`. `duration` is the SUM of every
87	    /// segment's — the total recorded, the paused stretches excluded because
88	    /// no file holds them.
89	    /// `mic_problem` is every segment's sentence joined
90	    /// (`RecordingResult.micProblem`), present when any segment's microphone
91	    /// was asked for and did not land — which is why, unlike R1, it can
92	    /// stand beside a `mic_path`: a second segment's failure leaves the
93	    /// first's file in place. `pauses` and `segments` are always present;
94	    /// `segments` has exactly one entry for a recording never paused.
95	    /// `unreadable` (#97) is present only when a segment was LEFT OUT because
96	    /// its movie would not probe, or its writer failed after it closed (#181):
97	    /// one entry per such segment, in order, with its movie's `path`, the
98	    /// `kept_files` still on disk and the `reason` — and, when its
99	    /// microphone file read (#181 item 2), `mic_path` and `mic_duration`,
100	    /// with `mic_media` and `mic_clip` from `leftOutIds` (one entry per
101	    /// left-out segment) when known. `camera` (spec §11 CAM-4) is present
102	    /// exactly when the result has one (`cameraFields`).
103	    static func recordingFields(
104	        _ result: RecordingResult, ids: [RecordingSegmentIds] = [],
105	        leftOutIds: [RecordingSegmentIds] = []
106	    ) -> [String: Any] {
107	        let first = result.segments[0]
108	        let movie = first.descriptor
109	        let total = result.segments.reduce(Ticks(0)) { $0 + $1.descriptor.duration }
110	        let segments = result.segments.enumerated().map { index, segment in
111	            segmentFields(segment, ids: index < ids.count ? ids[index] : nil)
112	        }
113	        var fields: [String: Any] = [
114	            "path": movie.path, "duration": total, "width": movie.width,
115	            "height": movie.height, "fps": [movie.fps.num, movie.fps.den],
116	            "has_audio": movie.hasAudio, "audio_tracks": movie.hasAudio ? 1 : 0,
117	            "mic_offset": first.micOffset, "stopped_by": stopReasonName(result.stoppedBy),
118	            "pauses": result.pauses, "segments": segments,
119	        ]
120	        if let mic = first.micDescriptor {
121	            fields["mic_path"] = mic.path
122	            fields["mic_duration"] = mic.duration
123	        }
124	        if let problem = result.micProblem { fields["mic_problem"] = problem }
125	        if let camera = result.camera {
126	            fields["camera"] = cameraFields(camera, id: result.choice.camera)
127	        }
128	        if !result.unreadable.isEmpty {
129	            fields["unreadable"] = result.unreadable.enumerated().map { i, left -> [String: Any] in
130	                var entry: [String: Any] = [
131	                    "path": left.moviePath, "kept_files": left.keptFiles,
132	                    "reason": left.error.localizedDescription,
133	                ]
134	                if let mic = left.micDescriptor {
135	                    entry["mic_path"] = mic.path
136	                    entry["mic_duration"] = mic.duration
137	                }
138	                let known = i < leftOutIds.count ? leftOutIds[i] : nil
139	                if let id = known?.micMedia { entry["mic_media"] = Int(id) }
140	                if let id = known?.micClip { entry["mic_clip"] = Int(id) }
141	                return entry
142	            }
143	        }
144	        fields.merge(idFields(ids.first)) { _, new in new }
145	        return fields

148	    /// One entry of `segments`: `path`, `duration`, `width`, `height`, `fps`
149	    /// (this FILE's, which on a variable-rate recording differs per segment
150	    /// — the top level's is the first segment's) and `started_at` (the
151	    /// screen's did-start, `startedAtFormatter`'s spelling), then `mic_path`,
152	    /// `mic_duration`, `mic_offset` (always, 0 with no microphone) and
153	    /// `mic_problem` on the top level's terms for THIS segment's files, and
154	    /// the four ids when known. A camera beside the screen (spec §11 CAM-10
155	    /// (6)) adds `camera_path`, `camera_duration` and `camera_offset` when
156	    /// the segment has a camera file, `camera_problem` and `camera_note`
157	    /// when set, and `camera_media` and `camera_clip` when known.
158	    static func segmentFields(
159	        _ segment: RecordingSegment, ids: RecordingSegmentIds? = nil
160	    ) -> [String: Any] {
161	        let movie = segment.descriptor
162	        var fields: [String: Any] = [
163	            "path": movie.path, "duration": movie.duration, "width": movie.width,
164	            "height": movie.height, "fps": [movie.fps.num, movie.fps.den],
165	            "started_at": startedAtFormatter.string(from: segment.startedAt),
166	            "mic_offset": segment.micOffset,
167	        ]
168	        if let mic = segment.micDescriptor {
169	            fields["mic_path"] = mic.path
170	            fields["mic_duration"] = mic.duration
171	        }
172	        if let problem = segment.micProblem { fields["mic_problem"] = problem }
173	        if let camera = segment.cameraDescriptor {
174	            fields["camera_path"] = camera.path
175	            fields["camera_duration"] = camera.duration
176	            fields["camera_offset"] = segment.cameraOffset
177	        }
178	        if let problem = segment.cameraProblem { fields["camera_problem"] = problem }
179	        if let note = segment.cameraNote { fields["camera_note"] = note }
180	        if let id = ids?.cameraMedia { fields["camera_media"] = Int(id) }
181	        if let id = ids?.cameraClip { fields["camera_clip"] = Int(id) }
182	        // The segment's cursor file beside its movie (spec §11 CU-18).
183	        if let url = segment.cursorURL { fields["cursor_path"] = url.path }
184	        if segment.cursorURL != nil, let image = segment.cursorImage {
185	            fields["cursor_image"] = image.rawValue
186	        }
187	        if let problem = segment.cursorProblem { fields["cursor_problem"] = problem }
188	        fields.merge(idFields(ids)) { _, new in new }
189	        return fields
190	    }

192	    /// `started_at`'s spelling: ISO 8601 in UTC to the millisecond
193	    /// (`2026-09-12T13:04:22.417Z`). The server reports no other date, so
194	    /// there was no spelling to match; UTC because the file's own name
195	    /// (`RecordingFiles.stem`) is already the local-time reading of the same
196	    /// instant and a second local spelling would say nothing new, and the
197	    /// fraction because the segments' offsets are measured in milliseconds.
198	    static let startedAtFormatter: ISO8601DateFormatter = {
199	        let formatter = ISO8601DateFormatter()
200	        formatter.formatOptions = [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds]
201	        formatter.timeZone = TimeZone(secondsFromGMT: 0)
202	        return formatter
203	    }()

205	    private static func idFields(_ ids: RecordingSegmentIds?) -> [String: Any] {
206	        var fields: [String: Any] = [:]
207	        if let id = ids?.media { fields["media"] = Int(id) }
208	        if let id = ids?.clip { fields["clip"] = Int(id) }
209	        if let id = ids?.micMedia { fields["mic_media"] = Int(id) }
210	        if let id = ids?.micClip { fields["mic_clip"] = Int(id) }
211	        return fields
212	    }

214	    static func stopReasonName(_ reason: StopReason) -> String {
215	        switch reason {
216	        case .stopped: return "stopped"
217	        case .userStopped: return "user_stopped"
218	        case .systemStopped: return "system_stopped"
219	        }
220	    }

222	    /// The `note` clause for a result some segment's microphone did not
223	    /// land for — the pictures are in the project and the answer must say
224	    /// what is missing. Over the JOINED problems, whose sentences name the
225	    /// segment's file when one was left behind. A voice-over has no picture:
226	    /// its problem — a microphone that stopped on its own — is said verbatim.
227	    static func microphoneNote(_ result: RecordingResult) -> String? {
228	        if result.isVoiceOver { return result.micProblem }
229	        return result.micProblem.map {
230	            "The picture landed without its microphone — the microphone file could not be "
231	                + "used: " + $0
232	        }
233	    }

235	    /// The result's own `note` clauses, in order: the segments left out as
236	    /// unreadable (#97), the left-out voices that landed (#181 item 2), the
237	    /// microphone's, then a camera's `problem` and `note`, verbatim (CAM-4),
238	    /// then every segment's camera sentences beside the screen
239	    /// (`cameraSegmentsNote`, CAM-10 (6)). Both doors append these after their
240	    /// own, on a landing that succeeded only.
241	    static func resultNotes(_ result: RecordingResult) -> [String] {
242	        [
243	            result.unreadableNote, result.leftOutVoiceNote, microphoneNote(result),
244	            result.camera?.problem, result.camera?.note,
245	            result.cameraSegmentsNote,
246	            // Every segment's cursor problem (spec §11 CU-18), last.
247	            result.cursorSegmentsNote,
248	        ].compactMap { $0 }
249	    }

251	    /// The ids a new project holds for every segment's files, read off its
252	    /// snapshot by path, SEGMENT BY SEGMENT — `untitled(around:)` placed
253	    /// them (the first picture as the document, the rest through
254	    /// `remainderPlacement`), so nothing here predicted an id, and a file
255	    /// the remainder landed as media alone (its sentence in the landing's
256	    /// `notes`) answers a `media` and no `clip`, which is the truth. A new
257	    /// project has no nest, so its top-level clips are the only clips there
258	    /// are.
259	    static func newProjectIds(
260	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument
261	    ) -> [RecordingSegmentIds] {
262	        let snapshot = document.project.snapshot
263	        return result.segments.map { segment in
264	            let media = landedMedia(for: segment.descriptor.path, in: snapshot)
265	            let micMedia = segment.micDescriptor.flatMap { landedMedia(for: $0.path, in: snapshot) }
266	            let cameraMedia = segment.cameraDescriptor.flatMap {
267	                landedMedia(for: $0.path, in: snapshot)
268	            }
269	            return RecordingSegmentIds(
270	                media: media, clip: media.flatMap { landedClip(of: $0, in: snapshot) },
271	                micMedia: micMedia, micClip: micMedia.flatMap { landedClip(of: $0, in: snapshot) },
272	                cameraMedia: cameraMedia,
273	                cameraClip: cameraMedia.flatMap { landedClip(of: $0, in: snapshot) })
274	        }
275	    }
276	
277	    /// The ids a DOCUMENT landing gives every segment — the placement's own
278	    /// four lists, the ids it predicted off the purely-applied trial (R1's
279	    /// contract: `next_id` before each op that mints) and the ones the panel
280	    /// selects, so the tool reports what the panel highlights. All four
281	    /// lists have ONE entry per segment, in order, nil where nothing was
282	    /// minted (`Placement`'s doc), so every one is indexed by SEGMENT and
283	    /// none is consumed by an iterator — the first shape here walked the two
284	    /// `mic…` lists as "segments with a microphone file" were met, and a
285	    /// voice that minted no clip then shifted every later segment's ids by
286	    /// one. Read BEFORE the commit, as R1 read the singulars, which is what
287	    /// lets `land()` keep `editResult`'s tail.
288	    static func documentIds(
289	        _ result: RecordingResult, placement: RecordingLanding.Placement
290	    ) -> [RecordingSegmentIds] {
291	        func entry(_ list: [UInt32?], _ k: Int) -> UInt32? { k < list.count ? list[k] : nil }
292	        return result.segments.indices.map { k in
293	            RecordingSegmentIds(
294	                media: k < placement.mediaIds.count ? placement.mediaIds[k] : nil,
295	                clip: entry(placement.clipIds, k), micMedia: entry(placement.micMediaIds, k),
296	                micClip: entry(placement.micClipIds, k),
297	                cameraMedia: entry(placement.cameraMediaIds, k),
298	                cameraClip: entry(placement.cameraClipIds, k))
299	        }
300	    }
301	
302	    /// The ids a DOCUMENT landing gives each left-out segment's voice (#181
303	    /// item 2): the placement's two left-out lists, one entry per
304	    /// `result.unreadable`, `micMedia` and `micClip` only.
305	    static func documentLeftOutIds(
306	        _ result: RecordingResult, placement: RecordingLanding.Placement
307	    ) -> [RecordingSegmentIds] {
308	        func entry(_ list: [UInt32?], _ i: Int) -> UInt32? { i < list.count ? list[i] : nil }
309	        return result.unreadable.indices.map { i in
310	            RecordingSegmentIds(
311	                micMedia: entry(placement.leftOutMicMediaIds, i),
312	                micClip: entry(placement.leftOutMicClipIds, i))
313	        }
314	    }
315	
316	    /// The ids a NEW project holds for each left-out segment's voice, read
317	    /// off its snapshot by trimmed path as `newProjectIds` reads the
318	    /// segments': a voice before the first segment is media with no clip.
319	    static func newProjectLeftOutIds(
320	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument
321	    ) -> [RecordingSegmentIds] {
322	        let snapshot = document.project.snapshot
323	        return result.unreadable.map { left in
324	            let micMedia = left.micDescriptor.flatMap { landedMedia(for: $0.path, in: snapshot) }
325	            return RecordingSegmentIds(
326	                micMedia: micMedia, micClip: micMedia.flatMap { landedClip(of: $0, in: snapshot) })
327	        }
328	    }
329	
330	    /// The media entry for `path`, matched TRIMMED because that is what the
331	    /// core stored (`RecordingLanding.addMedia`'s rule).
332	    private static func landedMedia(for path: String, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> UInt32? {
333	        let trimmed = path.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
334	        return snapshot.media.first(where: { $0.path == trimmed })?.id
335	    }
336	
337	    /// The first top-level clip whose source is `media`.
338	    private static func landedClip(of media: UInt32, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> UInt32? {
339	        snapshot.clips.first { clip in
340	            if case .media(let id, _, _) = clip.source { return id == media }
341	            return false
342	        }?.id
343	    }

356	/// Decision 4 (road map 3 §0): the PANEL asks for the grants, the tool never
357	/// does — the rule the speech grant's `canAsk` carried, for two grants.
358	/// What lives here is the READ of each grant, the STEP a press takes, the
359	/// pane URLs and the sentences — all pure: nothing here prompts or opens;
360	/// `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()`, `AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess` and
361	/// the pane's `NSWorkspace.open` are called by the recorder panel alone
362	/// (`RecorderPanelController+Grants.swift`), because a system prompt needs
363	/// a person in front of it. A press asks for Screen Recording ONCE and
364	/// opens the pane on every later press (spec §11 recording) — but only in
365	/// a launchd-owned launch: a shell-launched press always asks, because TCC
366	/// gives that prompt to the terminal (R0 q1). A denied or restricted
367	/// microphone opens its pane; `.notDetermined` asks.
368	///
369	/// **Both refusal sentences are COMPUTED, and end with `launchClause` when
370	/// it is non-empty** (R1 review, unjudged and upheld): R0 q1 measured that
371	/// a shell-launched Frame Job is attributed by TCC to the TERMINAL, so a
372	/// person who followed the pane sentence and granted Frame Job.app would have
373	/// granted the wrong application and be refused again with no way to tell
374	/// why. The pane sentence stays the PREFIX — `recording_proof.py` matches
375	/// on it — and the clause names the launching process's pid.
376	enum RecordingGrant {
377	    /// `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess()` — true when this PROCESS may
378	    /// capture. R0 q1: a shell-launched binary is attributed by TCC to the
379	    /// terminal, so from a proof this reads the terminal's grant, not the
380	    /// app's.
381	    static var screenRecordingGranted: Bool { CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess() }
382	
383	    /// The pane sentence alone — the prefix of `screenRecordingRefusal`.
384	    static let screenRecordingPaneSentence =
385	        "Screen Recording is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ "
386	        + "Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording, then relaunch."
387	
388	    static var screenRecordingRefusal: String { screenRecordingPaneSentence + launchClause }
389	
390	    /// Empty for an app launched by launchd (`open -a`, the Finder, the
391	    /// Dock — ppid 1, responsible for itself); otherwise the sentence that
392	    /// says whose grant this process is actually running under. `getppid()`
393	    /// is the cheapest true reading: R0 q1's `responsibility_get_pid_
394	    /// responsible_for_pid` is private API, and the parent is what TCC
395	    /// follows for a process launched from a shell.
396	    static var launchClause: String {
397	        let parent = getppid()
398	        guard parent != 1 else { return "" }
399	        return " This Frame Job was launched by another process (pid \(parent)), so the grant "
400	            + "that counts is that application's — the terminal's, for a shell launch; or "
401	            + "relaunch with open -a \"Frame Job\"."
402	    }

405	    /// `AVCaptureDeviceInput` is made: that initializer auto-prompts on

412	    /// read — `Transcriber.name(of:)`'s shape.
413	    static func name(of status: AVAuthorizationStatus) -> String {
414	        switch status {
415	        case .notDetermined: return "notDetermined"
416	        case .restricted: return "restricted"
417	        case .denied: return "denied"
418	        case .authorized: return "authorized"
419	        @unknown default: return "unknown"
420	        }
421	    }

423	    /// Names the status word and the one action that changes it: a
424	    /// `notDetermined` grant is asked for by pressing Record in the panel (the
425	    /// only place that may prompt), a denied or restricted one is turned on
426	    /// in System Settings. `launchClause` follows, on the same terms as the
427	    /// screen sentence's.

429	        let head = "The microphone is not granted to Frame Job (status: \(name(of: status))). "
430	        switch status {
431	        case .notDetermined:
432	            return head + "Press Record in File ▸ New Recording… once to grant it." + launchClause
433	        default:
434	            return head + "Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Microphone, "
435	                + "then relaunch." + launchClause

544	/// "Remove the camera's background when it lands" (road map "creator-jobs" CO8, spec §11
545	/// CO-81): Remove Background run over a finished recording's CAMERA clips as a follow-up to the
546	/// landing — never part of it — as its own undo step, "Remove Background", in AU-68's pattern
547	/// with no wait: the masks are wanted by the edit itself (`ensureMasks`, after every edit), so
548	/// nothing need be measured first. Both doors call `apply` right after the landing's commit and
549	/// before Enhance Voice and the polish (CU-101 (a)): the panel's two branches
550	/// (`RecorderPanelController+Landing.swift`) and the tool's `landAndEnhance`. On-device, so
551	/// never keyed (CJ-3). Names no `rc_*`; main thread.
552	enum RecordingCutout {
553	    /// The undo step's name, Clip ▸ Remove Background's.
554	    static let actionName = "Remove Background"
555	    /// The tool's `camera_cutout_error` when no camera clip took the cutout.
556	    static let noCameraSentence =
557	        "No camera clip landed on the timeline, so Remove Background did not run."
558	
559	    /// Every segment's camera file, in segment order; empty paths dropped, each path once. Pure.
560	    static func cameraPaths(of result: RecordingResult) -> [String] {
561	        var seen: Set<String> = []
562	        return result.segments.compactMap { $0.cameraDescriptor?.path }
563	            .map(RecordingLanding.trimmed)
564	            .filter { !$0.isEmpty && seen.insert($0).inserted }
565	    }
566	
567	    /// Every clip of the open container whose media is one of `paths`, that can be cut out
568	    /// (`CutoutStatus.canCutOut`) and has no cutout yet, in id order. Main.
569	    static func cameraClips(_ paths: [String], in document: ProjectDocument) -> [UInt32] {
570	        let wanted = Set(paths)
571	        guard !wanted.isEmpty else { return [] }
572	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
573	        return snapshot.clips.filter { clip in
574	            guard let media = snapshot.media(for: clip), wanted.contains(media.path) else {
575	                return false
576	            }
577	            return CutoutStatus.canCutOut(clip, in: snapshot) && clip.video?.cutout == nil
578	        }.map(\.id).sorted()
579	    }
580	
581	    /// One base `set_video {cutout}` per clip, the whole default cutout, as Clip ▸ Remove
582	    /// Background writes. Pure over the ids.
583	    static func ops(_ clips: [UInt32], in document: ProjectDocument) -> [ReelOp] {
584	        clips.map { .setVideo(clips: [$0], patch: VideoPatch(cutout: .some(CutoutProps()))) }
585	    }

587	    /// When the recording's choice asks for it, its camera clips cut out as ONE grouped step
588	    /// "Remove Background" (`performGroupedEdit`: a landing is not an AppKit event). Answers the
589	    /// clips the step was asked for, empty when the choice did not ask or no camera clip
590	    /// qualifies (the panel is then quiet; the tool answers `noCameraSentence`). Main.
591	    @discardableResult static func apply(_ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument)
592	        -> [UInt32]
593	    {
594	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
595	        guard result.choice.cameraCutout else { return [] }
596	        let clips = cameraClips(cameraPaths(of: result), in: document)
597	        guard !clips.isEmpty else { return [] }
598	        document.performGroupedEdit(actionName, ops(clips, in: document))
599	        return clips
600	    }

604	/// "Enhance the microphone when it lands" (road map "audio" AP6 part 3, spec
605	/// §11 AU-68, AU-69): Enhance Voice run over a finished recording's VOICE
606	/// clips as a follow-up to the landing — never part of it. The landing commits
607	/// at once and is unchanged (`RecordingLanding`, `untitled(around:)`, the step
608	/// names, the notes); Enhance follows as its own undo step, "Enhance Voice",
609	/// once the voice's loudness and speech caches exist, because neither can

611	///
612	/// The values and the pure decision are here: which files are the voice
613	/// (`voicePaths`), which clips they became (`voiceClips`), whether those are
614	/// measured (`isAnalysed`) and whether the document is in a state to take an

723	    /// One landing's follow: its document, its clips, the scope it landed in,
724	    /// when, and the timer.
725	    private final class Follow {
726	        weak var document: ProjectDocument?
727	        var clips: [UInt32]
728	        var scope: UInt32?
729	        var started: Date
730	        var timer: Timer?
731	
732	        init(document: ProjectDocument, clips: [UInt32], scope: UInt32?) {
733	            self.document = document
734	            self.clips = clips
735	            self.scope = scope
736	            self.started = Date()
737	        }
738	    }
739	
740	    /// The follows under way, by the document's `recipeKey` (never minted
741	    /// twice). A second landing into a document with a follow under way joins
742	    /// it: its clips are added and the clock and scope start again.
743	    private static var follows: [Int: Follow] = [:]
744	
745	    /// The panel's landing hands its result here once it has committed. A
746	    /// no-op unless the choice asked for it. Main.
747	    static func follow(_ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument) {
748	        guard result.choice.enhanceMicrophone else { return }
749	        let clips = voiceClips(of: result, in: document)
750	        let key = document.recipeKey
751	        if let pending = follows[key] {
752	            pending.clips = Array(Set(pending.clips + clips)).sorted()
753	            pending.scope = document.scope
754	            pending.started = Date()
755	            return
756	        }
757	        let follow = Follow(document: document, clips: clips, scope: document.scope)
758	        follows[key] = follow
759	        // `scheduledTimer` adds it in the DEFAULT mode: it waits out a drag.
760	        follow.timer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: checkInterval, repeats: true) {
761	            [weak document] timer in
762	            guard let document else {
763	                timer.invalidate()
764	                follows[key] = nil
765	                return
766	            }
767	            tick(document)
768	        }
769	    }
770	
771	    /// True only while a follow's timer runs for `document`. Main.
772	    static func isPending(_ document: ProjectDocument) -> Bool {
773	        follows[document.recipeKey] != nil
774	    }
775	
776	    /// The timer of `document`'s follow, nil with none — what the probe reads
777	    /// back after a step (P5). Main.
778	    static func timer(of document: ProjectDocument) -> Timer? {
779	        follows[document.recipeKey]?.timer
780	    }
781	
782	    /// One firing: decide, and on any step but `.wait` end the follow FIRST
783	    /// (the type doc), then act. Main.
784	    static func tick(_ document: ProjectDocument) {
785	        guard let follow = follows[document.recipeKey] else { return }
786	        let clips = present(follow.clips, in: document)
787	        let window = RecorderPanelController.editor(of: document)?.view.window
788	        let busy =
789	            isBusy(document, scope: follow.scope) || window == nil || window?.attachedSheet != nil
790	        let step = decide(
791	            clips: clips, analysed: isAnalysed(clips, in: document), busy: busy,
792	            elapsed: Date().timeIntervalSince(follow.started))
793	        guard step != .wait else { return }
794	        end(follow, key: document.recipeKey)
795	        switch step {
796	        case .enhance(let ids):
797	            guard let window else { return refuse(notReadySentence, in: document) }
798	            AudioMeasureDoor.enhanceLanded(document: document, clips: ids, window: window)
799	        case .giveUp:
800	            refuse(notReadySentence, in: document)
801	        case .drop, .wait:
802	            break
803	        }
804	    }
805	
806	    private static func end(_ follow: Follow, key: Int) {
807	        follow.timer?.invalidate()
808	        follows[key] = nil
809	    }

815	            userInfo: [
816	                "refusal": ReelRefusal(op: AudioMeasureDoor.Command.enhanceVoice.tool, reason: reason)
817	            ])
818	    }

98	    ///

101	    /// `ReelOp.documentLevelNames`) and its id read off the result; then,
102	    /// with `place`, the pictures as a sequence on ONE track by the two-try

107	    /// its probe runs against a project that does not hold the media yet,

123	    /// ONE new FRONT track named "Camera" and each camera clip at its screen

161	    /// make a clip of at all: it lands as media, with a sentence in `notes`.
162	    static func placement(
163	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument, place: Bool
164	    ) throws -> Placement {
165	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
166	        guard !document.isLiveEditing else {
167	            throw ReelCoreError(
168	                message: "A drag is in progress; the recording can be added when it ends.")
169	        }
170	        if result.isVoiceOver { return try voiceOverPlacement(result, in: document, place: place) }
171	        let scope = document.scope
172	        var trial = document.project
173	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
174	        var notes: [String] = []
175	
176	        var mediaIds: [UInt32] = []
177	        for segment in result.segments {
178	            mediaIds.append(try addMedia(segment.descriptor, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
179	        }
180	        var pictures: [Landed] = []
181	        if place {
182	            let stretches = try pictureStretches(
183	                of: result, mediaIds: mediaIds, in: trial, scope: scope)
184	            pictures = try addSequence(
185	                stretches, from: document.playhead, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops,
186	                notes: &notes)
187	            try addRipples(
188	                pictures.compactMap { $0.clip?.id }, of: result, scope: scope, to: &trial,
189	                ops: &ops)
190	        }
191	        let cameras = try addCameras(
192	            result, screenStarts: place ? segmentStarts(pictures.map { $0.at }, of: result) : nil,
193	            screenClips: split(pictures.map { $0.clip?.id }, of: result).segments,
194	            scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
195	        let microphones = try addMicrophones(
196	            voices(of: result), pictureStarts: place ? pictures.map { $0.at } : nil,
197	            scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
198	        let micMedia = split(microphones.media, of: result)
199	        let micClips = split(microphones.clips, of: result)
200	        return Placement(
201	            ops: ops, mediaIds: mediaIds,
202	            clipIds: place
203	                ? split(pictures.map { $0.clip?.id }, of: result).segments
204	                : mediaIds.map { _ in nil },
205	            micMediaIds: micMedia.segments, micClipIds: micClips.segments, notes: notes,
206	            leftOutMicMediaIds: micMedia.leftOut, leftOutMicClipIds: micClips.leftOut,
207	            cameraMediaIds: cameras.media, cameraClipIds: cameras.clips)

210	    // MARK: - The steps, each applied purely and read back
211	
212	    /// `add_media` applied purely; the id it minted, read off the result. A
213	    /// path already in the list is the documented IDENTITY
214	    /// (`core/src/edit_track.rs`), not a failure, and then the id is the
215	    /// entry's, matched by the TRIMMED path because that is what the core
216	    /// stored — `backgroundMedia(for:in:)`'s rule. The op stays in the list
217	    /// either way: `applying(_ ops:)` runs every later op after an identity,
218	    /// so one shape serves both cases and the undo step is one.
219	    static func addMedia(
220	        _ descriptor: MediaDescriptor, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
221	    ) throws -> UInt32 {
222	        let op = ReelOp.addMedia(descriptor: descriptor)
223	        ops.append(op)
224	        if let added = try trial.applying(op).project {
225	            trial = added
226	            guard let id = added.snapshot.media.last?.id else {
227	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(descriptor.path) was added and is not listed.")
228	            }
229	            return id
230	        }
231	        let path = trimmed(descriptor.path)
232	        guard let id = trial.snapshot.media.first(where: { $0.path == path })?.id else {
233	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(path) could not be added to the media list.")
234	        }
235	        return id
236	    }

238	    /// The two-try track rule over a SEQUENCE, for a `trial` that holds
239	    /// every `media`: all of them back to back on the front track of the
240	    /// open container, from `at`; if any one REFUSES there — the overlap
241	    /// rule is the only reason the core has — ALL of them on a new track in
242	    /// front of everything, from the same `at`. The sequence never splits: a
243	    /// recording whose first segment sits on one track and whose second on
244	    /// another would read as two recordings, so a refusal part-way discards
245	    /// the front track's half-placed trial whole (it was a copy) and starts
246	    /// the new track's from the trial that holds the media and no clip. The
247	    /// new track's id is `next_id` off the trial, and each clip's is
248	    /// `next_id` off the trial before its own `add_clip`.
249	    ///
250	    /// Only a REFUSAL (nil) falls through to the new track. An `Err` from
251	    /// the first attempt propagates: the caps are the same on either track,
252	    /// so a `try?` here — R1's shape — turned "too many clips" on a full
253	    /// document into a second attempt that added a track and then reported
254	    /// "too many tracks", the wrong cap, when the document was at both.
255	    /// `notes` takes the winning attempt's sentences (the same either way —
256	    /// a picture too short for a frame is too short on any track). The
257	    /// sequence is the whole stretch list, a left-out voice's gap included,
258	    /// so the rule sees every picture where it will land.
259	    private static func addSequence(
260	        _ stretches: [PictureStretch], from at: Ticks, scope: UInt32?,
261	        to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp], notes: inout [String]
262	    ) throws -> [Landed] {
263	        let container = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot
264	        if let front = container.tracks.last?.id {
265	            var attempt = trial
266	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
267	            var attemptNotes: [String] = []
268	            if let placed = try placeBackToBack(
269	                stretches, on: front, from: at, scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps,
270	                notes: &attemptNotes)
271	            {
272	                trial = attempt
273	                ops += attemptOps
274	                notes += attemptNotes
275	                return placed
276	            }
277	        }
278	        // Index 0 is the BACK of the stack (§6), so the count is the front.
279	        let addTrack = ReelOp.addTrack(index: container.tracks.count)
280	        let track = trial.snapshot.nextId
281	        guard let withTrack = try trial.applying(addTrack.scoped(scope)).project else {
282	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "A track for the recording could not be added.")
283	        }
284	        var attempt = withTrack
285	        var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = [addTrack]
286	        var attemptNotes: [String] = []
287	        guard
288	            let placed = try placeBackToBack(
289	                stretches, on: track, from: at, scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps,
290	                notes: &attemptNotes)
291	        else {
292	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "The recording could not be placed on a new track.")
293	        }
294	        trial = attempt
295	        ops += attemptOps
296	        notes += attemptNotes
297	        return placed
298	    }

300	    /// The clip `id` as the core reports it, read off the CONTAINER the ops
301	    /// are measured against — the nest's view while a scope is open, since
302	    /// a nested clip is not in the parent's `clips`. An id the trial does
303	    /// not list after its own `add_clip` accepted it is a throw, not a
304	    /// guess.
305	    static func clip(_ id: UInt32, in trial: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?) throws -> ClipSnapshot {
306	        let container = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot
307	        guard let clip = container.clips.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else {
308	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "Clip \(id) was placed and is not listed.")
309	        }
310	        return clip
311	    }
312	
313	    /// The container the clip ops are measured against: the nest's view
314	    /// while a scope is open (its tracks and clips at the top level, its
315	    /// `next_id` the parent's), else the trial itself. A scope naming a nest
316	    /// the trial has not got is a refusal, not a fallback — `clampViewState`
317	    /// clears one before anything reads it, so this arm is a race with an
318	    /// undo and the caller should not land on the timeline by accident.
319	    static func view(of trial: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?) throws -> ReelProject {
320	        guard let nest = scope else { return trial }
321	        guard let view = trial.scoped(nest) else {
322	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "The open nest (id \(nest)) is no longer in the project.")
323	        }
324	        return view
325	    }

329	    }

443	// of the core (road map 3, R2's toll): a PURE MOVE out of
444	// `RecordingLanding.swift` at the 400-line cap, holding `placeBackToBack`
445	// (a sequence of clips, each at the previous END as read back), `placeClip`
446	// (one `add_clip`, read back and stepped a frame up when the core snapped
447	// it under its floor — the inexact-rate rule the base file's header
448	// argues), `tooShortNote` (a file with no WHOLE frame inside it),
449	// `mediaEntry` and `milliseconds`. Every "what will the core snap this to"
450	// here is put to the core over the FFI — `ReelTime.snapToFrame` is
451	// `rc_time_snap_to_frame` — or read off a purely-applied result; nothing
452	// re-derives a frame in Swift, which is what makes the answers exact at
453	// 24981/1000 as at 30. Internal, not private, because the microphone file
454	// calls all of them and `private` does not cross a file.

456	import AppKit
457	
458	extension RecordingLanding {
459	    /// `media` as touching clips on `track`: the first at `at`, each later
460	    /// one at the previous clip's END as read off the trial after its
461	    /// `add_clip` — never computed here, because a sum over descriptor
462	    /// durations would be off-grid. Each is placed by `placeClip`, which
463	    /// reads the landed clip back and steps a frame up when the core snapped
464	    /// it under the previous end (an inexact rate; the header says why), so
465	    /// two clips meet at one tick or leave a sub-frame gap and never overlap
466	    /// (`core/src/transition.rs`: `overlap_of` answers none at zero length).
467	    /// A picture too short for a frame — the core's `whole_media_length`
468	    /// answers an `Err` for it, and that `Err` used to take the whole list
469	    /// down — lands as media alone, with its sentence in `notes`, and
470	    /// the sequence carries on from the same point. nil when any `add_clip`
471	    /// refuses — the caller decides what a refusal means — and a throw is
472	    /// the core's own sentence. A `.gap` (a left-out segment's voice, #181
473	    /// item 2) places nothing: its `Landed` has no clip and starts where the
474	    /// sequence had reached, and the next picture starts the gap's length
475	    /// later. Answers one `Landed` per stretch, in order.
476	    static func placeBackToBack(
477	        _ stretches: [PictureStretch], on track: UInt32, from at: Ticks, scope: UInt32?,
478	        to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp], notes: inout [String]
479	    ) throws -> [Landed]? {
480	        var placed: [Landed] = []
481	        var at = at
482	        for stretch in stretches {
483	            let id: UInt32
484	            switch stretch {
485	            case .gap(let length):
486	                placed.append(Landed(clip: nil, at: at))
487	                at += length
488	                continue
489	            case .picture(let media):
490	                id = media
491	            }
492	            let file = try mediaEntry(id, in: trial, scope: scope)
493	            let fps = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas.fps
494	            if let note = tooShortNote(file, at: fps) {
495	                notes.append(note)
496	                placed.append(Landed(clip: nil, at: at))
497	                continue
498	            }
499	            guard
500	                let landed = try placeClip(
501	                    id, on: track, at: at, notBelow: at, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops)
502	            else { return nil }
503	            placed.append(Landed(clip: landed, at: landed.start))

505	        }
506	        return placed
507	    }

509	    /// `add_clip` of `media` on `track` at `at`, applied purely and READ
510	    /// BACK, and never landed below `floor` (≤ `at`): the core snaps the
511	    /// start to the nearest frame, and at an inexact canvas rate the
512	    /// nearest frame to a clip's end can be UNDER it — the end is a sum of
513	    /// two grid points, which is not one — so a landing under the floor is
514	    /// discarded whole and the add is made again at `floor` plus a frame,
515	    /// whose nearest frame is at or above the floor and within a frame of
516	    /// it. What comes back therefore satisfies `floor ≤ start ≤ at + frame`:
517	    /// touching, or a sub-frame gap at an inexact rate, never an overlap
518	    /// (which the rule would accept and dress as a transition). A landing
519	    /// outside that band after the second try is a throw, not a guess. nil
520	    /// is the core's refusal — an overlap the rule will not accept — and
521	    /// the op is appended and the trial advanced only for the clip returned.
522	    static func placeClip(
523	        _ media: UInt32, on track: UInt32, at: Ticks, notBelow floor: Ticks, scope: UInt32?,
524	        to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
525	    ) throws -> ClipSnapshot? {
526	        precondition(at >= floor, "a clip is asked for at or above its floor")
527	        let frame = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas.fps.frameDuration
528	        for requested in [at, floor + frame] {
529	            let op = ReelOp.addClip(track: track, media: media, at: requested)
530	            let id = trial.snapshot.nextId
531	            guard let next = try trial.applying(op.scoped(scope)).project else { return nil }
532	            let landed = try clip(id, in: next, scope: scope)
533	            if landed.start < floor { continue }
534	            guard landed.start <= at + frame else {
535	                throw ReelCoreError(
536	                    message: "Clip \(id) landed at \(landed.start), more than a frame past \(at).")
537	            }
538	            trial = next
539	            ops.append(op)
540	            return landed
541	        }
542	        throw ReelCoreError(
543	            message: "Clip \(trial.snapshot.nextId) could not be placed at or after \(floor).")
544	    }

546	    /// The sentence for a media the core cannot make a clip of, or nil: a
547	    /// timed media with no WHOLE frame inside it is an `Err` to
548	    /// `whole_media_length` (`core/src/edit_clip.rs`) — "no duration" at

550	    /// measured a real 2 ms microphone file. The test IS the core's: a clip

556	    static func tooShortNote(_ file: MediaSnapshot, at fps: Fps) -> String? {
557	        guard file.kind != .image,

561	        }

564	    }

566	    /// The media entry `id` names in `trial` — the document's one list, which
567	    /// a nest's view shares (`core/src/scope.rs`). An id the trial's own
568	    /// `add_media` answered and does not list is a throw.
569	    static func mediaEntry(_ id: UInt32, in trial: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?) throws
570	        -> MediaSnapshot
571	    {
572	        let container = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot
573	        guard let media = container.media.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else {
574	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "Media \(id) was added and is not listed.")

582	    static func milliseconds(_ ticks: Ticks) -> String {
583	        String(format: "%.1f", Double(ticks) / (Double(ReelTime.perSecond) / 1000))

625	    /// 0. With several, two voices on one track can neither overlap — a
626	    /// refusal, or worse a sub-frame overlap the rule ACCEPTS as a
627	    /// transition, minting a cross dissolve between two halves of one
628	    /// recording — nor be placed late (the same wrong sound as R1's negative
629	    /// start put at 0), so the floor for voice `k` is the previous voice's
630	    /// END, and a start below it is head-trimmed to it by the same dance.
631	    /// The floor is READ off the trial, never computed: the previous clip's
632	    /// end is on the frame grid because the core snapped its start and its
633	    /// length, and a sum over descriptor durations would not be. (At an
634	    /// inexact rate even that end is not a grid point, and `placeClip` steps
635	    /// the add up a frame when the core snaps under it.)
636	    ///
637	    /// The track is added on the attempt of the FIRST voice that takes a
638	    /// frame, and kept only when that voice lands: a voice that mints no
639	    /// clip discards its attempt whole, so a recording with no placeable
640	    /// voice adds no empty track. Its id is `next_id` off the trial at that
641	    /// moment, unchanged by a discarded attempt.
642	    static func addMicrophones(
643	        _ voices: [Voice], pictureStarts: [Ticks?]?, scope: UInt32?,
644	        to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp], notes: inout [String]
645	    ) throws -> (media: [UInt32?], clips: [UInt32?]) {
646	        precondition(
647	            pictureStarts.map { $0.count == voices.count } ?? true,
648	            "one picture start per voice")
649	        var media: [UInt32?] = []
650	        for voice in voices {
651	            if let mic = voice.descriptor {
652	                media.append(try addMedia(mic, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
653	            } else {
654	                media.append(nil)
655	            }
656	        }
657	        let none: [UInt32?] = voices.map { _ in nil }
658	        guard let starts = pictureStarts else { return (media, none) }
659	        var track: UInt32?
660	        var clips: [UInt32?] = []
661	        var floor: Ticks = 0
662	        for (k, voice) in voices.enumerated() {
663	            guard let id = media[k], let start = starts[k] else {
664	                clips.append(nil)
665	                continue
666	            }
667	            var attempt = trial
668	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
669	            let on: UInt32
670	            if let added = track {
671	                on = added
672	            } else {
673	                on = attempt.snapshot.nextId
674	                let addTrack = ReelOp.addTrack(index: 0, name: microphoneTrackName)
675	                guard let withTrack = try attempt.applying(addTrack.scoped(scope)).project
676	                else {
677	                    throw ReelCoreError(message: "A track for the microphone could not be added.")
678	                }
679	                attempt = withTrack
680	                attemptOps.append(addTrack)
681	            }
682	            guard
683	                let placed = try addMicrophoneClip(
684	                    id, on: on, pictureAt: start, offset: voice.offset, floor: floor,
685	                    scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps, notes: &notes)
686	            else {
687	                clips.append(nil)
688	                continue
689	            }
690	            trial = attempt
691	            ops += attemptOps
692	            track = on
693	            clips.append(placed.id)
694	            floor = placed.end
695	        }
696	        return (media, clips)
697	    }

699	    /// One voice's clip on `track`, at `pictureAt − offset` and never below
700	    /// `floor` — 0 for the first voice, the previous voice's end after it.
701	    /// nil, with a sentence in `notes`, for a voice that gets no clip; the
702	    /// trial and the ops are advanced only for a clip returned.
703	    ///
704	    /// **The sign.** `offset` is the screen's did-start minus the
705	    /// microphone's, in ticks; positive means the picture began AFTER the
706	    /// microphone, so the microphone's content LEADS and its clip starts
707	    /// that much earlier than the picture's. R0 measured it centred near
708	    /// zero with a 35 ms scatter (road map 3, R0 q6b) and a different number
709	    /// at every resume (q7), and the landing applies each segment's measured
710	    /// number — never a constant, never the first segment's.
711	    ///
712	    /// **When that start is below the floor** — the picture at 0 with the
713	    /// microphone ahead of it, or a later voice whose picture began less
714	    /// than its offset after the previous voice ended — the clip cannot
715	    /// start there: below 0 there is no timeline, below the previous voice's
716	    /// end there is a clip, and placing it AT the floor would leave the
717	    /// voice LATE by the difference. So the head is trimmed off instead, and
718	    /// it stays one grouped edit: `add_clip` at the floor, `trim_start` to
719	    /// the landed start + head (the core sets the start there and advances
720	    /// `in` by the same amount — `core/src/edit_clip.rs`), `move_clip` back
721	    /// by what the trim advanced, read off the trimmed clip (the head, at
722	    /// an exact rate; at an inexact one the grid point nearest it). A
723	    /// `slip` would be the one-op spelling and cannot be used: the clip
724	    /// covers its whole media, so the slip's clamp reduces it to nothing.
725	    /// The head is the core's own snap of the shortfall
726	    /// (`ReelTime.snapToFrame`, the rounding every time argument gets), so a
727	    /// start within half a frame of the floor makes no trim and the two ops
728	    /// are not sent — the core's snap of that start lands it on the floor —
729	    /// while a start further below is trimmed rather than left to the snap,
730	    /// because the core would snap it to the frame BELOW the floor: at 0
731	    /// clamped up and late by a frame, above 0 a one-frame overlap the rule
732	    /// accepts as a transition. Limit: the grid is the picture's frame — at
733	    /// 60 fps 16.7 ms — so the alignment is exact to half a frame and no
734	    /// finer.
735	    ///
736	    /// **Every step is read back, and two things are decided by what comes
737	    /// back** (the R2 review). `trim_start` clamps its `to` at a frame
738	    /// before the clip's end, so a voice no longer than its head — an 80 ms
739	    /// file whose picture began 100 ms after it — used to be trimmed to a
740	    /// one-frame sliver and then moved back INTO the previous voice, which
741	    /// `move_clips` refused: `applying(_ ops:)` still answered non-nil (the
742	    /// add and the trim had changed something), the trial "succeeded", and
743	    /// the commit ran a refused op inside its undo step with the sliver
744	    /// sitting late. Now the trimmed clip's start is compared with the
745	    /// core's own snap of the requested `to`, and a start that is not it is
746	    /// the clamp: the voice is wholly under its head, mints NO clip, and its
747	    /// sentence names the file. And the moved clip must land exactly where
748	    /// the core's snap of the delta says, at or above the floor, or the
749	    /// throw names the file — a refused op can never ride a committed list.
750	    /// At an INEXACT rate the move's landing can be a tick under a floor
751	    /// that is a grid point (the delta and the trim round separately; grid
752	    /// points are not closed under addition), which the rule would accept
753	    /// and dress as a transition, so that one case is done once more a
754	    /// frame up with a frame more head: the content stays aligned to the
755	    /// tick, the voice starts a sub-frame gap after the previous one, and
756	    /// its first frame past the head is the price — the documented limit of
757	    /// such a rate, beside the pictures' own sub-frame gap.
758	    static func addMicrophoneClip(
759	        _ media: UInt32, on track: UInt32, pictureAt: Ticks, offset: Ticks, floor: Ticks,
760	        scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp], notes: inout [String]
761	    ) throws -> ClipSnapshot? {
762	        let file = try mediaEntry(media, in: trial, scope: scope)
763	        let fps = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas.fps
764	        if let note = tooShortNote(file, at: fps) {
765	            notes.append(note)
766	            return nil
767	        }
768	        let start = pictureAt - offset
769	        let head = start < floor ? ReelTime.snapToFrame(floor - start, fps: fps) : 0
770	        guard head > 0 else {
771	            guard
772	                let placed = try placeClip(
773	                    media, on: track, at: max(start, floor), notBelow: floor, scope: scope,
774	                    to: &trial, ops: &ops)
775	            else {
776	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(file.path) could not be placed on its track.")
777	            }
778	            return placed
779	        }
780	        let frame = fps.frameDuration
781	        for (at, head) in [(floor, head), (floor + frame, head + frame)] {
782	            var attempt = trial
783	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
784	            guard
785	                let placed = try headTrimmed(
786	                    media, file: file, on: track, at: at, head: head, floor: floor, fps: fps,
787	                    scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps)
788	            else {
789	                notes.append(underNote(file, head: head, floor: floor))
790	                return nil
791	            }
792	            if placed.start >= floor {
793	                trial = attempt
794	                ops += attemptOps
795	                return placed
796	            }
797	        }
798	        throw ReelCoreError(
799	            message: "\(file.path) could not be placed clear of the previous microphone clip.")
800	    }
801	
802	    /// The dance once, on `trial`: the add at `at` (never under `floor`),
803	    /// the trim to the landed start + `head`, the move back by what the trim
804	    /// advanced. nil when the trim clamped — the voice is wholly under its
805	    /// head — with the trial left as it was; every other surprise is a
806	    /// throw naming the file. The clip returned may still sit a tick under
807	    /// the floor at an inexact rate, which the caller reads.
808	    static func headTrimmed(
809	        _ media: UInt32, file: MediaSnapshot, on track: UInt32, at: Ticks, head: Ticks,
810	        floor: Ticks, fps: Fps, scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
811	    ) throws -> ClipSnapshot? {
812	        guard
813	            let added = try placeClip(
814	                media, on: track, at: at, notBelow: floor, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops)
815	        else {
816	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(file.path) could not be placed on its track.")
817	        }
818	        let trim = ReelOp.trimStart(clip: added.id, to: added.start + head)
819	        let promisedTrim = ReelTime.snapToFrame(added.start + head, fps: fps)
820	        guard let trimmed = try trial.applying(trim.scoped(scope)).project,
821	            try clip(added.id, in: trimmed, scope: scope).start == promisedTrim
822	        else { return nil }
823	        let advanced = promisedTrim - added.start
824	        let move = ReelOp.moveClip(clips: [added.id], delta: -advanced)
825	        let promisedStart = promisedTrim + ReelTime.snapToFrame(-advanced, fps: fps)
826	        guard let moved = try trimmed.applying(move.scoped(scope)).project else {
827	            throw ReelCoreError(
828	                message: "\(file.path) could not be moved back by its \(milliseconds(advanced)) ms head.")
829	        }
830	        let landed = try clip(added.id, in: moved, scope: scope)
831	        guard landed.start == promisedStart, landed.source.sourceIn == advanced else {
832	            throw ReelCoreError(
833	                message: "\(file.path) landed at \(landed.start) with \(landed.source.sourceIn) "
834	                    + "trimmed, not at \(promisedStart) with \(advanced).")
835	        }
836	        trial = moved
837	        ops += [trim, move]
838	        return landed
839	    }
