841	    /// The sentence for a voice wholly under its head.
842	    private static func underNote(_ file: MediaSnapshot, head: Ticks, floor: Ticks) -> String {
843	        let clear = floor == 0 ? "the start of the timeline" : "the previous microphone clip"
844	        return "\(file.path) was added to the media list without a clip: less than a frame of "
845	            + "it would remain after the \(milliseconds(head)) ms head that keeps it clear of "
846	            + "\(clear)."
847	    }
848	}
849	// app/Sources/RecordingLanding+VoiceOver.swift — where a finished VOICE-OVER
850	// goes (spec §11 recording, "A voice-over is a recording with no picture",
851	// #99).
852	//
853	// A voice-over is an ordinary `RecordingResult` whose every segment's
854	// `descriptor` is an `.m4a` (`isVoiceOver`). `placement(_:in:place:)` forwards
855	// it here after its live-edit guard, and the rule is not the picture rule:
856	// every file lands on ONE new BACK track named "Microphone" — where a screen
857	// recording's microphone lands — touching, from the playhead, in the one
858	// grouped edit both doors commit as "Add Recording". Never the front track,
859	// and never an existing Microphone track: no rule says which track is "the"
860	// voice track. The placing is `placeBackToBack`'s (`+Placing`), so every clip
861	// is read back and a file under a frame lands as media with its
862	// `tooShortNote`; the track is kept only when at least one clip landed on it.
863	//
864	// A NEW project needs nothing here: `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)` makes
865	// the first file the document (audio-only, 1920×1080 at the chosen rate) and
866	// `remainderPlacement` puts the later files touching it on its one track.
867	
868	import AppKit
869	
870	extension RecordingLanding {
871	    /// PURE, main thread: the voice-over's ops and predicted ids. Every
872	    /// file's `add_media` in order (document-level, unscoped); then, with
873	    /// `place`, on a trial copy, `add_track` at index 0 named
874	    /// `microphoneTrackName` and every file back to back from the playhead
875	    /// on it. A refusal on that new, empty track is thrown by name. The
876	    /// track and its clips are kept only when at least one clip landed —
877	    /// every file under a frame adds media and notes alone, and then no
878	    /// `add_track` is even tried, so a document at the track cap does not
879	    /// throw for a track nothing would land on. `clipIds` has
880	    /// one entry per segment; the two `mic…` lists are all nil (a
881	    /// voice-over's voice IS its descriptor); the two left-out lists have
882	    /// one nil per `unreadable` entry. The ops come back unscoped, the
883	    /// container ops stamped by the caller's door as for any landing.
884	    static func voiceOverPlacement(
885	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument, place: Bool
886	    ) throws -> Placement {
887	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
888	        let scope = document.scope
889	        var trial = document.project
890	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
891	        var notes: [String] = []
892	        var mediaIds: [UInt32] = []
893	        for segment in result.segments {
894	            mediaIds.append(try addMedia(segment.descriptor, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
895	        }
896	        var clipIds: [UInt32?] = mediaIds.map { _ in nil }
897	        let fps = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas.fps
898	        let shortNotes = try mediaIds.map {
899	            tooShortNote(try mediaEntry($0, in: trial, scope: scope), at: fps)
900	        }
901	        let canLand = shortNotes.contains { $0 == nil }
902	        if place && !canLand {
903	            notes += shortNotes.compactMap { $0 }
904	        } else if place {
905	            var attempt = trial
906	            let track = attempt.snapshot.nextId
907	            let addTrack = ReelOp.addTrack(index: 0, name: microphoneTrackName)
908	            guard let withTrack = try attempt.applying(addTrack.scoped(scope)).project else {
909	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "A track for the voice-over could not be added.")
910	            }
911	            attempt = withTrack
912	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = [addTrack]
913	            guard
914	                let placed = try placeBackToBack(
915	                    mediaIds.map { PictureStretch.picture($0) }, on: track,
916	                    from: document.playhead, scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps,
917	                    notes: &notes)
918	            else {
919	                throw ReelCoreError(
920	                    message: "The voice-over could not be placed on its new Microphone track.")
921	            }
922	            if placed.contains(where: { $0.clip != nil }) {
923	                trial = attempt
924	                ops += attemptOps
925	                clipIds = placed.map { $0.clip?.id }
926	            }
927	        }
928	        let none: [UInt32?] = mediaIds.map { _ in nil }
929	        let leftOut: [UInt32?] = result.unreadable.map { _ in nil }
930	        return Placement(
931	            ops: ops, mediaIds: mediaIds, clipIds: clipIds, micMediaIds: none, micClipIds: none,
932	            notes: notes, leftOutMicMediaIds: leftOut, leftOutMicClipIds: leftOut)
933	    }
934	}

954	extension RecordingLanding {
955	    /// The undo step's name for `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`'s

966	    /// paused recording's later segments, with or without microphones.

968	    /// segment is the document and stays under the undo; what the step takes

974	    /// document, and the step takes the camera back.

978	    static let cameraMicrophoneActionName = "Add Camera and Microphone"

980	    /// Which name `untitled(around:)`'s remainder edit takes. For ONE

990	        if result.segments.count == 1 {
991	            let voice =
992	                result.segments[0].micDescriptor != nil
993	                || result.unreadable.contains(where: { $0.micDescriptor != nil })

995	                return voice ? cameraMicrophoneActionName : cameraActionName

1003	    /// Everything a fresh untitled document does NOT already hold, for
1004	    /// `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`, whose `makeProject` placed the
1005	    /// FIRST segment's picture at 0 on track 1 before anything else could
1006	    /// run: segments 2…n's media and their pictures on that same track from
1007	    /// clip 1's end, then every segment's microphone by the floor rule. nil
1008	    /// when there is nothing to add — one segment, no microphone, no camera
1009	    /// and no ripples (`wantsRipples` with a cursor not in the picture, CU-31).
1010	    /// `placement(_:in:place:)` cannot serve it — the first picture's
1011	    /// `add_media` would be the documented identity and its `add_clip` at 0
1012	    /// would meet its own clip on the front track, refuse, and put the whole
1013	    /// sequence a SECOND time on a new track. The answer reads as a whole
1014	    /// landing: `mediaIds[0]` and `clipIds[0]` name the picture the document
1015	    /// holds.
1016	    ///
1017	    /// Clip 1 is the FIRST clip whose source is the first segment's media,
1018	    /// and the later pictures go on ITS track from ITS end — read off the
1019	    /// document, not assumed to be track 1 at 0. That is exact for the one
1020	    /// caller: `makeProject` places exactly one clip. A document holding the
1021	    /// same media in several clips has no single answer here, and this
1022	    /// method does not pretend to one — it is `untitled(around:)`'s, not a
1023	    /// general "add the rest of a recording to a document" op. The later
1024	    /// pictures take no two-try rule: a refusal on a fresh document's one
1025	    /// track is not a track choice to fall back from but something wrong
1026	    /// with a file, and is thrown by name.
1027	    ///
1028	    /// **Without clip 1** — `makeProject` tolerates a first picture the core
1029	    /// refuses (a media with no duration) and opens the file in the Media
1030	    /// tab — nothing on the timeline says where the recording is, so the
1031	    /// remainder lands as MEDIA ONLY, `place: false`'s shape, with a
1032	    /// sentence per file in `notes`. The first shape here placed every
1033	    /// voice against a picture at 0, R1's one-segment fallback, which with
1034	    /// several voices stacked each one under the last (the floor rule
1035	    /// trimming a whole voice off) — a wrong sound where a Media-tab list
1036	    /// is at least an honest one.
1037	    ///
1038	    /// **A left-out segment's readable voice** (#181 item 2) is a stretch:
1039	    /// after clip 1 a gap the later pictures skip and a voice at its start;
1040	    /// BEFORE clip 1, which is the document at 0, media only with
1041	    /// `leadingVoiceNote`; without clip 1, media only with `unplacedNote`.
1042	    ///
1043	    /// **A camera beside the screen** (spec §11 CAM-10 (4)) lands after the
1044	    /// later pictures and before the voices, by `addCameras` against each
1045	    /// segment's picture start — clip 1's included — on ONE new track in
1046	    /// front of the pictures', laid out with its segment's picture; without
1047	    /// clip 1, as media only with
1048	    /// `unplacedNote`.
1049	    ///
1050	    /// **The ripples** (CU-31 (c)) go on clip 1 and the later pictures right
1051	    /// after those are placed (`addRipples`); without clip 1 there are none.
1052	    static func remainderPlacement(
1053	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument
1054	    ) throws -> Placement? {
1055	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
1056	        let hasMicrophone = result.segments.contains { $0.micDescriptor != nil }
1057	        let hasLeftOutVoice = result.unreadable.contains { $0.micDescriptor != nil }
1058	        let hasCamera = result.segments.contains { $0.cameraDescriptor != nil }
1059	        let more = result.segments.count > 1 || hasMicrophone || hasLeftOutVoice || hasCamera
1060	        guard more || wantsRipples(result) else { return nil }
1061	        let path = trimmed(result.descriptor.path)
1062	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
1063	        guard let mediaId = snapshot.media.first(where: { $0.path == path })?.id else {
1064	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(path) is not in the document's media list.")
1065	        }
1066	        let first = snapshot.clips.first { clip in
1067	            if case .media(let id, _, _) = clip.source { return id == mediaId }
1068	            return false
1069	        }
1070	        let scope = document.scope
1071	        var trial = document.project
1072	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
1073	        var notes: [String] = []
1074	        var mediaIds = [mediaId]
1075	        for segment in result.segments.dropFirst() {
1076	            mediaIds.append(try addMedia(segment.descriptor, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
1077	        }
1078	        var starts: [Ticks?]?
1079	        var clips: [UInt32?] = result.stretches.map { _ in nil }
1080	        if let first = first {

    s = prod[n]['inputSchema']

    for k in ['kind', 'region', 'rate', 'fps', 'at', 'focus', 'text', 'shape', 'groups', 'ranges', 'clips']:

            p = dict(s['properties'][k])
            d = p.pop('description', '')

docs/guide/mcp.md:451:| `auto_zoom` | Plans screencast zooms from screen recordings' cursor files and applies them as one undo step (**Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**): `clip` or `clips`, and `zoom`, `lead`, `stay`, `follow`, `typing`, `replace`, `motion_blur`, `from`, `to`. Each zoom is an ordinary action; each zoomed clip whose own `motion_blur` is 0 is given `motion_blur` (0–1, 0.5 by default, the sheet's Motion blur; 0 gives none). Answers `visits`, `added`, `replaced`, `dropped`, `closed_at_cut`, `bases_set`, `blurred` and `actions`. A clip placed smaller than the canvas is refused (nest it and call inside the nest with `set_scope`), as is one that plays reversed. Read on this Mac, no key. |
docs/guide/mcp.md:592:| `get_media_analysis` | The hard cuts (`kind: "shots"`) in one media file, or in the part of it one clip plays, with clip and timeline times for a clip; or where a person is found (`kind: "masks"`): the runs of frames whose person masks agree on whether a person is there, with the masks' size and frame counts, never the masks themselves; or every face (`kind: "faces"`): ten samples a second, each with its faces' boxes, roll and yaw and how wide and open the mouth is, left to right and with no names. A row with one face is about 176 bytes, so one answer holds about five minutes of samples (four with a clip): ask for a longer file in `from`/`to` windows. Or the people and the regions the eye goes to (`kind: "subjects"`): ten samples a second, each with its people's boxes (head and shoulders) and its salient regions' boxes, left to right, about 177 bytes a row, as faces'; **View ▸ Show Subjects** draws what faces and subjects have found for the selected clip. Or what is heard (`kind: "sound_events"`): every 0.75 s, how sure Apple's sound classifier is of laughter, applause, cheering, a crowd, music and speech over the next 1.5 s of the file's first sound track, as numbers from 0 to 1 (empty where the sound has ended). These are hints, not findings: no group has been checked against labelled recordings yet. It needs a file with sound (an audio file works) and is refused for a clip that plays in reverse. Found on this Mac, kept in the project's cache, no key and nothing uploaded. A cut inside a gradual dissolve or a single flash frame is not reported; a dissolve between flat-coloured pictures (slides, title cards) can show as one cut. A clip whose `set_video` `cutout` is set (**Clip ▸ Remove Background**, the Picture tab's Background section) has its masks made as soon as it is set, without this call, and draws them: the person alone, in the preview, `render_frame` and every export. The preview draws a frame whose mask is not made yet whole; `render_frame` waits up to 30 s for it and an export waits for every mask it draws. A picture's masks are not this tool's (an image has no moving picture): `analyze_cutout` answers them. |
docs/guide/screen-recording.md:22:| **Preview** | With **Source** set to **Camera**, or with **Record the camera too** ticked, a live picture of the chosen camera at the chosen format, under Format. It's shown as the movie will record it: not mirrored, the whole picture fitted inside. The row appears only then. | — |
docs/guide/screen-recording.md:73:The camera starts as soon as the panel shows **Camera**, and the **Preview** under Format shows its live picture. Because it's already running, it has settled at its frame rate by the time recording begins, and its light stays on while the panel shows **Camera**. Choosing a display or another source (unless **Record the camera too** is ticked there), or closing the panel, turns it off. The preview changes with the camera and format you choose. Instead of the picture it reads "No camera is connected." with no camera, "The preview shows once Frame Job may use the camera." until you've allowed the Camera permission (showing the panel never asks for it, pressing Record does), or the reason the camera couldn't start. Choosing **Camera** again or reopening the panel tries again. **The panel stays up** while a camera records, as it does for a voice-over: nothing on screen is filmed. Its controls lock, the meter stays live, the footnote shows ● or ❚❚ and the elapsed time, Record reads **Stop**, and a **Pause** / **Resume** button appears beside it. If you close the panel, the recording carries on.
docs/guide/screen-recording.md:94:Each camera clip stays an ordinary clip: you can move it, or choose another layout from **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸**. If a tool records a camera beside the screen while the panel is up, the panel's **Preview** reads "The camera is recording." until it ends.
docs/guide/screen-recording.md:254:**Motion blur.** With the clip's **Motion Blur** above 0 (the Transform section, see [Motion blur](motion-and-transitions.md#motion-blur)), a moving pointer is drawn streaked along its path across the shutter, in the preview, `render_frame` and every export; a still pointer is drawn as it is. The click ripples stay sharp.
docs/guide/screen-recording.md:283:| **Motion blur** | Gives each zoomed clip a 50 % [motion blur](motion-and-transitions.md#motion-blur) (a 180° shutter), so the zooms and pans blur along their movement. A clip that already has a Motion Blur keeps its own. | on |
docs/guide/screen-recording.md:285:The sheet reads the cursor files first ("Reading cursor files…"), then says what Zoom would do, for example "5 zooms in 2 visits." and, when some planned zooms meet an action already on the clip, "1 dropped where an action is already set." It says so instead when a clip can't be planned. Frame Job remembers Zoom, Arrive, Stay, Follow, Replace and Motion blur for next time, but only once you change one; Zoom on typing is never remembered.
docs/guide/screen-recording.md:297:*Agents:* `auto_zoom` plans and applies the same zooms, with the sheet's settings as arguments; its `motion_blur` (0–1, 0.5 by default) is the sheet's Motion blur, and its answer's `blurred` counts the clips it gave one.
docs/guide/screen-recording.md:401:With `source: "camera"`, Frame Job records a camera on its own, with no screen, into `Camera Recording <date> at <time>.mov`. The camera is the one `camera` names, or else the default camera: the Mac's preferred camera, then the first built-in camera, then the first one connected. It records at the camera's best format (the largest size wider than tall that runs at 30 fps or more, at that format's highest frame rate), or at the format `camera_format` names. A blank or null `camera_format` means best, and a format the camera doesn't have is refused with a list of the camera's formats. `microphone: true` adds the default microphone as a second file, as for a screen recording. The arguments `display`, `window`, `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows`, `keys`, `cursor`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing` and `rate` are refused by name, and `camera` and `camera_format` are refused with `source: "voice_over"`. An unknown camera is refused with a list of every camera connected, and with none connected the answer is "No camera is connected." A camera recording needs the **Camera** permission (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Camera**), which is read and never asked for, like the others. The recording starts once the camera has settled at its frame rate (up to a second), and `seconds` counts from its first frame. A camera recording made this way takes the camera from the panel's preview: while it runs, the panel's **Preview** reads "The camera is recording." and the picture comes back when the recording ends. The answer carries `camera` with the camera's `name`, `id` and `format` (for example `1760x1328@30`), plus `problem` when the camera stopped on its own and `note` when it hadn't settled at its rate by the time recording began. The note repeats both. The movie has no sound of its own, so `has_audio` is false. In a new project, the canvas is the file's size at the format's frame rate.
docs/guide/screen-recording.md:415:With `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` or `speed_up_typing`, the call then runs `auto_zoom`, `add_shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing`, in that order, on the recording's screen clips, each as its own undo step as in [When it lands](#when-it-lands). An agent's runs use those tools' defaults (Zoom ×2, Lead 0.6 s, Stay 2.5 s, Follow on, Motion blur 50 %; bottom and dark overlays; ×4 for stretches of 3 s or more, Keep pitch on), never the sheets' remembered values, and `speed_up_typing` waits up to 5 minutes for the speech. The answer then also carries each one's own answer under its name, or a sentence under `auto_zoom_error`, `shortcut_overlays_error` or `speed_up_typing_error`: no screen clip with a cursor file landed, the project busy (or the speech not detected) within 5 minutes, the call stopped first, or the tool's own refusal, which an agent is told rather than asked (a speed-up that leaves a clip silent above ×12 applies and says so in `audio_note`). `project` is read after them. They're checked right after `enhance`, before any permission, in that order: `place: false` is refused first ("auto_zoom: true plans on the landed screen clips, so it needs place: true."), then `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` without `keys: "shortcuts"` ("speed_up_typing: true needs keys: \"shortcuts\" — without it the cursor file records no typing to speed up.").
136:- `record_screen` never asks for the Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera or Input
258:`import_captions`, `export_captions`, `relay_captions` and `record_screen` take no `scope`
260:whatever nest `set_scope` has open (`record_screen` places its clip there),
637:| `record_screen` | Records a display or window for 1–600 `seconds` and lands it as media (**File ▸ New Recording…**), records the microphone alone with `source: "voice_over"`, or a camera alone with `source: "camera"` (and `camera` to choose one, `camera_format` its format); with `source: "screen"` and `camera`, records that camera beside the screen on a Camera track in front, laid out by `camera_layout` (the panel's **Layout**: `corner_square`, the bottom-right corner, by default; `corner_rounded`, `corner_circle`, `side_by_side`, `camera_full`), and `camera_cutout: true` (the panel's Remove the camera's background box) runs Remove Background on the camera clips as its own undo step right after the landing, answering `camera_cutout` or `camera_cutout_error`; both need `camera` and `place: true` and are refused with `voice_over` and `camera`. `enhance: true` then runs `enhance_voice` on the microphone's clips as its own undo step once their sound is analysed, answering `enhance` or `enhance_error`. `keys: "shortcuts"` (the panel's **Record shortcuts**) writes each shortcut, spelled, and a time-only typing mark for every other key into the cursor files; it needs the Input Monitoring grant and is refused with `voice_over` and `camera`. `cursor` (the panel's **Cursor**) is `separate` — the pointer kept out of the movie and drawn by Frame Job, with `show_clicks` landing the clips with click ripples — or `in_picture`; absent, `separate`; refused with `voice_over` and `camera`. `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` (the panel's **When it lands:** boxes) then run `auto_zoom`, `add_shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` on the screen clips, in that order, each its own undo step after the landing and any `enhance`, answering each one's answer or its `…_error`; each needs `place: true`, the last two `keys: "shortcuts"`, and all three are refused with `voice_over` and `camera`. |
28:| **Cursor** | **Separate** keeps the pointer and the click ring out of the movie: the recording's cursor file records them, and Frame Job draws the pointer on the clip, where its **Cursor** section can restyle it (see [The cursor](#the-cursor)). **In the picture** lets macOS draw the pointer into the movie, as before. It's greyed out, keeping its value, with **Camera** or **Microphone Only**. | **Separate** |
29:| **Show Clicks** | With Cursor **In the picture**, draws a ring around each mouse click into the movie. With Cursor **Separate**, nothing is drawn into the movie: the recording's clips land with click ripples turned on (**Clicks: Ripple** in their Cursor section). | Off |
210:| Its cursor | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.fjcursor` | Beside every screen recording's movie (a display, a window or a picked window), one per stretch between pauses: where the pointer was about 120 times a second, every click and scroll, and how the recorded area sat on the screen. With Cursor set to In the picture, the pointer is drawn into the movie as well. If the file can't be written, the recording still lands and the panel's note says why |
237:| **Show cursor** | Draws the pointer from the file over the clip. On by default. | on, off |
248:With an action selected, **Size** and **Ripple size** animate across it. **Show cursor**, **Style**, **Clicks** and **Ripple color** switch at the action's end. **Smoothing**, **Hide when idle** and **Polish** belong to the clip, not to an action: their rows show ⊘ and they always change the clip itself. A clip with no cursor settings yet gets them the first time you change any row but Smoothing or Hide when idle with an action selected, so Size and Ripple size can animate rather than jump. Selecting clips that disagree shows a row mixed. **Reset** puts every row back to its default.
256:**What a recording lands with.** With **Cursor** set to **Separate**, macOS draws no pointer into the movie, the cursor file says the pointer is not in the picture, and the landed clip gets a **Cursor** section, with the pointer drawn as recorded. With **Show Clicks** on as well, the clips land with **Clicks** set to **Ripple**, in the same undo step as the recording (in a new project whose only other change is that, the undo name is "Cursor Clicks"). Nothing else is set: **Polish** is one click away. With **In the picture**, the pointer is in the movie, its cursor file says so, and the clip shows no **Cursor** section, so nothing is drawn twice.
